# CampusOS

Cloud-native, multi-tenant School Operating System. Replaces 8–15 disconnected school software systems with one platform.

## Project Status

**Phase 2 Cycle 11 (P2-11 Transportation Advanced, M61 .1) — COMPLETE pending peer review across three sub-cycles (2026-05-11).** P2-11a (Fleet Maintenance + Fuel + Driver Hours, 8 tables + 30 endpoints) shipped at `3ae014c`. P2-11b (Route Generation Pipeline + Ad-Hoc Trips + Contracted Routes, 7 tables + 24 endpoints + Scheduling Solver stub fallback) shipped at `4872e46`. **Phase 2 Cycle 10 (P2-10 Food Service Advanced, M63 .1) — REVIEW-P2C10 ROUND 2 fixes applied (2026-05-11).** Round 2 verdict against `9ca4aa5` + `730b2b3` returned **FAIL** with 3 new BLOCKING in `PreorderService` (P2-10a Round 1 fixes at `730b2b3` confirmed PASS — the Round 2 reviewer cache-busted recipe/inventory/transfer/staff-meal and verified every Round 1 fix, but found the same broad-STAFF + cross-school patterns hadn't been propagated to the P2-10b preorder paths). The Round 2 fix commit lands all 3 BLOCKINGs + 7 new pinned regression tests. **BLOCKING fixes**: (1) **Preorder student/guardian authorization school-scoped** — `PreorderService.assertCanOrderForStudent` STUDENT branch SQL rewrites from `WHERE s.id = $1::uuid AND ps.person_id = $2::uuid` to `WHERE s.school_id = $1::uuid AND s.id = $2::uuid AND ps.person_id = $3::uuid`. GUARDIAN branch SQL adds `JOIN sis_students s ON s.id = sg.student_id AND s.school_id = $1::uuid` to the inner JOIN. `buildVisibilityFilter` STUDENT + GUARDIAN sub-queries mirror the same school predicate. A student/guardian whose platform identity also exists at another school can no longer order through THIS tenant against a foreign-school sis_students row. (2) **FSM admin on-behalf validates studentId in current tenant** — `assertCanOrderForStudent` admin path no longer blanket-bypasses; the FSM admin branch (school admin OR holds FDS-006:write) now runs `SELECT 1 AS ok FROM sis_students WHERE school_id = $1::uuid AND id = $2::uuid LIMIT 1` and throws `BadRequestException('studentId does not match a student in this school')` on miss. A School A FSM admin providing a School B student UUID can no longer mint a preorder with `school_id = $A` + `student_id = $B`. (3) **Generic STAFF → FDS-006:write across PreorderService** — constructor now takes `PermissionCheckService`. New `isFsmAdmin(actor)` helper short-circuits on `actor.isSchoolAdmin` then calls `permissionCheckService.hasAnyPermissionInTenant(actor.accountId, schoolId, ['fds-006:write'])`. Every callsite that previously checked `personType === 'STAFF'` rewrites to `await this.isFsmAdmin(actor)`: `assertCanManageWindows` (window CRUD), `confirmPreorder` admin gate, `cancelPreorder` admin override path, `generateProductionReport` admin gate, `buildVisibilityFilter` list-all bypass, `createPreorder` window-gate bypass, `assertCanOrderForStudent` admin on-behalf gate. Mirrors the P2-10a Round 1 fix shape across the 4 other food-service services. **Test coverage**: vitest 518 → **525 passing across 26 spec files** (+7 new Round 2 pinned regression tests across 3 REVIEW-P2C10 ROUND 2 describe blocks: BLOCKING 1 × 2 (STUDENT branch school-scope SQL + GUARDIAN sub-query school-scope SQL); BLOCKING 2 × 1 (admin on-behalf with cross-school studentId refused 400 + INSERT never fires); BLOCKING 3 × 4 (STAFF without FDS-006 refused on createWindow + confirmPreorder + generateProductionReport + window-gate-bypass on-behalf)). **CI parity green**: format:check + lint:logs (708 files clean) + api build clean + web build clean + vitest 525/525. No schema migrations in Round 2 — the only schema delta in this cycle is the FDS-006 catalogue entry added in Round 1. Awaiting Round 3 verdict before tagging `p2c10-complete`. See `REVIEW-P2C10-CHATGPT.md` for the Round 2 triage table + per-fix verification trail.

**Phase 2 Cycle 10 (P2-10 Food Service Advanced, M63 .1) — REVIEW-P2-10a ROUND 1 fixes applied (2026-05-11).** Round 1 of REVIEW-P2C10-CHATGPT (against the P2-10a closeout commit `a91b192`) returned **FAIL** with 4 BLOCKING + 4 MAJOR. The Round 1 fix commit lands all 4 BLOCKING + the 1 actionable MAJOR (5) with 11 new pinned regression tests so the contracts cannot regress. **BLOCKING fixes**: (1) **Recipe ingredient school-scope** — `RecipeService.addIngredient` FOR UPDATE lock rewrites from `WHERE id = $1::uuid FOR UPDATE` to `WHERE id = $1::uuid AND school_id = $2::uuid FOR UPDATE`; `updateIngredient` + `deleteIngredient` JOIN rewrites from `JOIN fds_recipes r ON r.id = i.recipe_id` to `JOIN fds_recipes r ON r.id = i.recipe_id AND r.school_id = $2::uuid`; new `assertInventoryItemBelongsToSchool(tx, inventoryItemId)` helper validates `input.inventoryItemId` against `fds_inventory_items.school_id = $tenant.schoolId` on every add + update path. A School A actor providing a School B `recipeId` or cross-school `inventoryItemId` now collapses to 404 / 400 instead of corrupting the School B recipe's allergen + cost rollups. (2) **Inventory level movement school-scope** — Both `InventoryService.movement` + `InventoryService.stocktake` existing-level lock SQL rewrite from `FROM fds_inventory_levels l JOIN fds_inventory_items i WHERE l.group_id = $1 AND l.item_id = $2 FOR UPDATE OF l` to `FROM fds_inventory_levels l JOIN fds_inventory_groups g ON g.id = l.group_id JOIN fds_inventory_items i ON i.id = l.item_id WHERE l.group_id = $1::uuid AND l.item_id = $2::uuid AND g.school_id = $3::uuid AND i.school_id = $3::uuid FOR UPDATE OF l`. A School A actor providing a `(groupId, itemId)` pair that exists in School B can no longer lock + mutate the foreign-school level row + write a phony audit transaction. (3) **Durable `fds.inventory.low` via OutboxService** — new `deterministicInventoryLowEventId(transactionId)` helper produces a v5-shaped UUID via `sha256(transactionId + ':fds.inventory.low:v1')` with the v5 marker nibbles set (same shape as P2-4a `deterministicPayrollEventId` + P2-6 `deterministicCreditNoteEventId`). The emit path moves INSIDE `executeInTenantTransaction` via `OutboxService.enqueueInTx`, so the outbox row commits with the parent tx and `OutboxPublisherWorker` publishes when the broker recovers. The post-tx `emitInventoryLow` helper that called `KafkaProducerService.emit` is removed. `InventoryService` constructor now takes `OutboxService` + `PermissionCheckService` instead of `KafkaProducerService`. (4) **Generic STAFF → FDS-006:write** — new `FDS-006 (Food Service Administration)` permission code added to `permissions.json` (catalogue 350 → 352). New shared helper `assertFsmAdminScope(permCheck, actor, surface)` in `apps/api/src/food-service/fsm-scope.ts` short-circuits on `actor.isSchoolAdmin` then calls `permissionCheckService.hasAnyPermissionInTenant(accountId, schoolId, ['fds-006:write'])`. Every `assertCanManage()` in `RecipeService` / `InventoryService` / `TransferService` / `StaffMealService` rewrites from `personType === 'STAFF'` to the new helper. `seed-iam.ts` grants Staff role `FDS-006:read+write`; admin tiers reach via `everyFunction`. Teacher / Parent / Student NOT granted. Cache rebuilt + verified live: admin/principal/vp/counsellor hold `fds-006:write`; teacher/parent/student all FALSE. **MAJOR 5 fix**: `StaffMealService.patch` UPDATE now predicates on both `id` AND `school_id` (was id-only + relied on the school-scoped reload to 404 a cross-school hit, but the mutation already landed). **Test coverage**: vitest 507 → **518 passing across 26 spec files** (+11 new pinned regression tests across 5 REVIEW-P2-10a ROUND 1 describe blocks: BLOCKING 1 × 3 (lock SQL school-scope + cross-school inventoryItemId 400 + JOIN school predicate); BLOCKING 2 × 1 (lock SQL JOINs + 2 school predicates); BLOCKING 3 × 2 (deterministicInventoryLowEventId stability + v5-shape + outbox-not-kafka emit path); BLOCKING 4 × 4 (recipe/inventory/transfer/staff-meal STAFF without FDS-006 refused); MAJOR 5 × 1 (UPDATE includes school_id)). **MAJORs 6 + 7 + 8 carried to Phase 2 punch list per reviewer's gate decision**: defensive transfer level joins (recommendation-class polish — transfer creation already validates groups + item against current school), DB-level trigger on `fds_inventory_transactions` for immutability (joins the broader "immutability triggers" punch list with Cycle 8 + 10 + 21 audit logs), `fds.staff_meal.settled` event for payroll integration (depends on payroll integration contract). **CI parity green**: format:check + lint:logs (708 files clean) + api build clean + web build clean + vitest 518/518. **Phase 2 Cycle 9 (P2-9 Sub Marketplace) — REVIEW-P2C9 ROUND 1 fixes applied (2026-05-11).** Round 1 of REVIEW-P2C9-CHATGPT (against the P2-9c closeout commit `9e9b133`) returned **FAIL** with 4 BLOCKING + 4 MAJOR. The Round 1 fix commit lands all 4 BLOCKING + 2 actionable MAJORs (5 + 6) + 14 new pinned regression tests so the contracts cannot regress. **BLOCKING fixes**: (1) **Permission split — SUB-001 self-service vs SUB-002 marketplace administration** — new `SUB-002 (Substitute Marketplace Administration)` permission code added to `permissions.json`. Every service-layer `hasMarketplaceScope` / `hasAdminScope` helper (`substitute-profile`, `school-pool`, `job-posting`, `pay-rate`, `cancellation-policy`, `assignment`, `session-note`, `rating`) now gates on **`sub-002:write`** only (was `sch-004:write` and/or `sub-001:write`, both of which generic Staff holds). Staff role retains `SUB-001:read+write` for self-service (own profile, availability, preferences, accept jobs, own notes, own ratings) but loses `SCH-004:write`; only School Admin / Platform Admin hold `sub-002:*` via `everyFunction` until a dedicated Sub Coordinator role lands. Catalogue: ~349 → ~350. (2) **Job posting school-scoped reference validation** — `JobPostingService.post()` `hr_employees` lookup now predicates `WHERE school_id = $1::uuid AND id = $2::uuid` (was `WHERE id = $1::uuid`); timetable slot lookup adds `WHERE s.school_id = $1::uuid AND s.id = $2::uuid` (slots carry `school_id` directly per Cycle 5 migration 016); `SELECT_JOB_BASE` JOIN on `hr_employees` now carries `AND e.school_id = j.school_id`. Foreign-school absent-teacher and foreign-school timetable slot UUIDs now return friendly 400s before any insert lands. (3) **Worker school-scoping (AcceptanceExpiryWorker + JobNotificationWorker)** — `AcceptanceExpiryWorker.tickForTenant` UPDATE now JOINs through `sub_job_postings j` and predicates `j.school_id = $1::uuid`, so a tick under School A context cannot expire School B's PENDING notifications in a multi-school tenant pool. `JobNotificationWorker.tickForTenant` ripe-job SELECT predicates `j.school_id = $1::uuid`. **Phase 2 Cycle 8 — Round 1 fix log preserved below for review trail.**

**Phase 2 Cycle 8 (P2-8 Athletics Advanced, M66 .1) — REVIEW-P2-8 ROUND 1 fixes applied (2026-05-10).** Round 1 against the combined P2-8a (`62ba7aa`) + P2-8b (`7d7c93d`) state returned **FAIL** with **6 BLOCKING + 4 MAJOR**. The Round 1 fix commit lands all 6 BLOCKING + 3 actionable MAJORs (1 + 2 + 3) with 8 new pinned regression tests so the contracts cannot regress. **BLOCKING fixes**: (1) **Durable outbox for `ath.equipment.replacement_charge`** — `EquipmentService.returnCheckout` no longer uses best-effort `KafkaProducerService.emit` post-commit; instead calls `OutboxService.enqueueInTx(tx, ...)` INSIDE the same tx that flips the checkout to RETURNED + DAMAGED/LOST. The envelope `eventId` is a **deterministic v5-shaped UUID** keyed on `checkoutId` via the new `deterministicReplacementChargeEventId(checkoutId)` helper (same shape as P2-4a `deterministicPayrollEventId` + P2-6 `deterministicCreditNoteEventId`) — outbox retries land the same envelope every time and the Cycle 6 billing consumer's idempotency catches redelivery cleanly. (2) **Equipment checkout assignee tenant-validation** — new `EquipmentService.assertAssigneeInCurrentSchool(client, personId)` helper joins through `sis_students.platform_student_id → platform_students.person_id` for current-school students AND through `hr_employees.person_id` for current-school staff. Bogus / cross-school iam_person UUIDs return `400 "assignedToPersonId does not match a student or staff member in this school"` BEFORE the INSERT lands. Closes the attack path where a School A AD could issue equipment to an arbitrary platform person UUID. (3) **Conference catalogue + cross-school schedule authority split** — `ConferenceService.create` + `patch` re-gated from `hasConferenceScope` (school AD) to new `hasCatalogueAdminScope` (PLATFORM-scope `sys-001:admin` OR `ath-003:admin` only — uses Cycle 31 `permissionCheckService.resolvePlatformScope()` + `hasAnyPermission` so the gate is solely the PLATFORM-scope assignment). `addScheduleEntry` requires either platform-tier authority OR `homeSchoolId === tenant.schoolId OR awaySchoolId === tenant.schoolId` — a tenant AD cannot fabricate a "School B vs School C" game. Plus `seasonId` is now validated through `ath_seasons → ath_programmes.school_id` chain. (4) **Durable outbox for `ath.highlight_clip.portfolio_link_requested`** — `GameStreamService.addClipToPortfolio` now uses `OutboxService.enqueueInTx` inside the same tx as the `added_to_portfolio = true` flip. Deterministic event_id via `deterministicHighlightLinkEventId(clipId)`. (5) **Durable outbox for `ath.official.assignment.completed`** — `OfficialService.transitionAssignment` COMPLETED branch now enqueues to outbox in same tx. Deterministic event_id via `deterministicAssignmentCompletedEventId(assignmentId)`. (6) **Platform official profile mutation gate** — new `OfficialService.hasMarketplaceAdminScope(actor)` checks the actor holds `sys-001:admin` or `ath-003:admin` at PLATFORM scope specifically (via `resolvePlatformScope` + `hasAnyPermission`). `createProfile`, `updateProfile`, `createAvailability` re-gated from `hasOfficialAdminScope` (school AD via tenant-scope `ath-003:write`) to `hasMarketplaceAdminScope`. School ADs can still post assignments + submit ratings under `ath-003:write`, but they cannot mutate the canonical platform record. **MAJOR fixes**: (1) Team media `seasonId` validated through `ath_seasons → ath_programmes.school_id` chain in `TeamMediaService.createAsset`, with cross-validation against `programmeId` when both supplied. (2) **Under-13 COPPA gate on highlight clip self-consent** — `GameStreamService.recordClipConsent` resolves the student's date_of_birth via the `sis_students → platform_students → iam_person.date_of_birth` chain when the actor is the student themself; ages < 13 are refused with `403 "COPPA: students under 13 cannot self-consent…"` and must defer to a linked guardian or admin. (3) **Official contact field DTO strip** — `OfficialService.listProfiles` + `getProfileById` now take an actor and run through new `stripContactsIfNeeded(actor, dto)` which clears `contactEmail` + `contactPhone` for readers without `ath-003:write` (assignment authority). MAJOR 4 (per-public/admin DTO split for memberships/schedules) accepted as recommendation-class polish — current shape is still sound. **Test coverage**: vitest 428 → **436 passing across 24 spec files** (+8 new BLOCKING regression tests covering: BLOCKING 1 outbox emit + deterministic event_id v5-shape, BLOCKING 2 cross-school assignee rejection, BLOCKING 3 school-AD-rejected-on-catalogue-create + tenant-AD-rejected-on-cross-school-fabrication + platform-admin-can-create UNIQUE catch, BLOCKING 4 portfolio-link emit deterministic event_id, BLOCKING 5 assignment-completed emit deterministic event_id, BLOCKING 6 school-AD-rejected-on-platform-profile-create + platform-admin-can-create). Existing `EquipmentService.returnCheckout` + `OfficialService.transitionAssignment` + `GameStreamService.addClipToPortfolio` tests rewritten to use new `makeOutbox()` stub instead of `makeKafka()`, so the durable contract is locked across the entire suite. **CI parity green**: format:check + lint:logs (679 files clean) + API + web build + vitest 436/436. Awaiting Round 2 verdict before tagging `p2c8-complete`. See `REVIEW-P2-8-CHATGPT.md` for the full triage table + per-fix verification trail.

**Phase 2 Cycle 8 (P2-8 Athletics Advanced, M66 .1) — original Round 1 build (2026-05-10).** Sub-cycle structure: 18 ERD tables across 2 sub-cycles, ~42 endpoints. **P2-8a — Equipment + Conferences + Media — already shipped at `62ba7aa`** (9 tenant tables in migration 130, ~20 endpoints, emits `ath.equipment.replacement_charge` to Cycle 6 family billing on DAMAGED/LOST returns). **P2-8b — Streaming + Officials + Recruiting (this commit)** — 7 tenant tables in migration 131 + **2 platform tables** in Prisma migration `20260510_add_p2c8_athletics_officials` (per ADR-063 officials are portable across schools and live above the tenant boundary), ~22 endpoints, 1 new Kafka emit (`ath.official.assignment.completed`) + 1 cross-cycle emit (`ath.highlight_clip.portfolio_link_requested` to Cycle 24 portfolio). **Three structural keystones in P2-8b:** (1) **PLATFORM OFFICIALS PER ADR-063** — `platform.platform_official_profiles` (UNIQUE(person_id) + non-empty sports[] + base_fee + certification fields) + `platform.platform_official_availability` (UNIQUE(profile, date, start_time) + multi-column `window_chk` enforcing all-day-or-specific-window). Tenant `ath_official_assignments.official_profile_id` is a soft UUID per ADR-001/020 — the Step 4 service validates platform existence before the tenant INSERT. The OfficialService's `listProfiles` queries the platform schema via `tenantPrisma.getPlatformClient()` so the marketplace browse is not tenant-scoped. (2) **HIGHLIGHT CLIP CONSENT GATING (ADR-068)** — athletic events are public performances by default but adding a clip to a student portfolio requires consent. Schema enforces via multi-column `portfolio_consent_chk` on `ath_highlight_clips` (`added_to_portfolio = false OR consent_status = 'CONSENTED'`). Service `addClipToPortfolio` locks the row, validates consent, sets the flag, and emits `ath.highlight_clip.portfolio_link_requested` for the Cycle 24 portfolio consumer to materialise the `pfl_portfolio_items` row. Consent recording is open to student-self / linked guardian / AD-admin (admin override for COPPA cases where under-13 students cannot legally consent). (3) **BIDIRECTIONAL OFFICIAL RATINGS** — `ath_official_ratings.rater_type` 2-value CHECK SCHOOL_RATES_OFFICIAL plus OFFICIAL_RATES_SCHOOL with UNIQUE(assignment_id, rater_type) caps each direction at one row per assignment. Both sides have voice on the marketplace reputation score. Refused on non-COMPLETED assignments. **STUDENT-OWNED RECRUITING PROFILES** — `ath_recruiting_profiles` is the **fifth student-input write surface** in CampusOS after Cycle 11.1 wellbeing / Cycle 12 reading logs / Cycle 17 service hours / Cycle 24 portfolio items. Service-layer row-scope: student-self can edit own profile but NOT the `coachRecommendation` field (coach/admin only — student should not author their own recommendation letter); coach/admin can edit any profile; guardians read-only on linked children's profiles; non-linked actors see only `is_published=true` profiles. Review notes: `P2C6-REVIEW-NOTES.md`. **P2-6a shipped steps 1–7 + 10 — schema (4 migrations), seed (idempotent), 10 NestJS services, 4 controllers, 21 net new endpoints, 3 Kafka emit topics, 1 new Kafka consumer (LunchAccountConsumer).** **14 net new tenant base tables** across 4 migrations (123 + 124 + 125 + 126 — the plan's 17-table count includes 3 tables that already exist from Cycle 6: `pay_fee_categories`, `pay_fee_schedules`, `pay_payment_plans`). Tenant base table count: 481 → **495**. **3 IMMUTABLE tables** per ADR-010 (`pay_credit_notes`, `pay_payment_reversals`, `pay_lunch_account_balance_transfers`) — service layer exposes ONLY list / get / create paths with NO update or delete methods. Schema-side belt-and-braces: UNIQUE(payment*id) on `pay_payment_reversals` enforces one reversal per payment at the DB layer. **Three structural keystones**: (1) **FINANCIAL AID FUND POOL ATOMIC DECREMENT (KEYSTONE)** — `FinancialAidService.reviewApplication` APPROVE path locks both the application AND the parent programme rows FOR UPDATE inside one tenant tx, validates `awardAmount ≤ fund_remaining`, INSERTs the award + decrements `fund_remaining` + stamps `award_id` on the application atomically. UNIQUE(student, program, academic_year) on awards is the schema-side dedup against double-issuing. Programme cannot oversell its fund under concurrency. (2) **PAYMENT REVERSAL OFFSETTING-LEDGER KEYSTONE** — `ReversalService.reverse` is IMMUTABLE per ADR-010. Locks invoice FIRST then payment FOR UPDATE (consistent ordering with `PaymentService.pay` + `RefundService.issue` to prevent deadlock); writes an offsetting CHARGE pay_ledger_entries row to nullify the original PAYMENT credit; flips payment to FAILED; recomputes invoice status from the refund-aware paid formula (PAID → OVERDUE / PARTIAL / SENT); emits `pay.payment.reversed` for the Cycle 26 GLConsumer. UNIQUE(payment_id) on the reversal table catches double-reversal. **Phase 2 Cycle 4 sub-cycle a (P2-4a Payroll, M80 .1) — REVIEW-P2-4a ROUND 1 fixes applied (2026-05-09).** Round 1 against `1a5c3e8` returned **FAIL** with 3 BLOCKING + 4 MAJOR. The Round 1 fix commit lands all 3 BLOCKING + the actionable MAJOR (#2 lifecycle lockstep) + 4 new keystone unit tests. **BLOCKING fixes**: (1) **Durable outbox for `hr.payroll.processed`** — `markPaid()` no longer uses best-effort `KafkaProducerService.emit` post-commit; instead calls `OutboxService.enqueueInTx(tx, ...)` INSIDE the same tx that flips period + records to PAID. Each row writes one `platform.platform_outbox` envelope; the existing Cycle 31 `OutboxPublisherWorker` polls + publishes durably and stamps `published_at` on success. A Kafka outage leaves the outbox row pending (failed_at populated, attempt_count bumped); the worker retries on the next poll until MAX_OUTBOX_ATTEMPTS. The envelope `eventId` is a **deterministic v5-shaped UUID** keyed on `payroll_record_id` via the new `deterministicPayrollEventId(payrollRecordId)` helper (same shape as P2C2 `deterministicStepEventId` and Cycle 4 `deterministicCoverageEventId`) — outbox retries land the same envelope every time and the GLConsumer dedupes on `platform_event_consumer_idempotency`. (2) **`markPaid()` requires every record APPROVED** — service runs an in-tx `SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS n WHERE status <> 'APPROVED'` before any UPDATE; rejects with `400 "Cannot mark paid: N payroll record(s) are not yet APPROVED. Run /pay-periods/:id/approve first."` when any non-APPROVED row remains. The subsequent `UPDATE hr_payroll_records SET status='PAID' WHERE … AND status='APPROVED'` is the schema-side belt-and-braces (was previously `status IN ('DRAFT','APPROVED')` — silently bypassed approval). Both check + UPDATE run under the period's `FOR UPDATE` lock so concurrent admins cannot race past it. (3) **New permission code `HR-010 Payroll Management`** — added to `permissions.json` (catalogue 501 → **504**). Staff role grants `HR-010:read+write` via `seed-iam.ts`; School Admin / Platform Admin pick up admin tier through `everyFunction`. Controller endpoints re-gated: pay-grade + pay-period admin reads moved from `hr-003:read` (held by Teacher / Staff for Cycle 4 leave + own payslips) to `hr-010:read`; admin writes (process / approve / mark-paid / pay-grade CRUD) re-gated to `hr-010:admin`. Service-layer `PayrollService.isAdmin`, `PayGradeService.assertAdmin`, `SalaryReviewService.isAdmin` re-pointed at `hr-010`. **Self-service payslip endpoints (`/hr/payroll/records`, `/hr/payroll/records/:id`, `/hr/payroll/me/payslips`) keep `hr-003:read`** because the service layer binds non-admin readers to `actor.employeeId` — that's the actual access boundary, identical to the P2C3 pattern. Live-verified IAM distribution: Teacher / Parent / Student have HR-003:read but **NO HR-010** so payroll admin views are now invisible to them. **MAJOR #2 fix**: new tenant migration `112_hr_pay_period_lockstep.sql` (splitter-safe DROP IF EXISTS + ADD pattern, idempotent) tightens two CHECK constraints on `hr_pay_periods`: `processed_chk` (OPEN/CLOSED ⇒ processed_at + processed_by both NULL; PROCESSING/PAID ⇒ both NOT NULL) + `paid_chk` (status<>'PAID' ⇒ paid_at + paid_by both NULL; status='PAID' ⇒ both NOT NULL). Live verified — direct INSERT of status='PAID' with NULL paid_at rejected by paid_chk. **Test coverage**: 12 → **14 keystone unit tests** — new tests cover the in-tx COUNT-then-reject path, the OutboxService.enqueueInTx call shape including topic/sourceModule/deterministic eventId/full GLConsumer payload contract, the deterministic event-id helper's stability + v5 shape, controller permission-metadata regression (admin reads on hr-010, self-service on hr-003). Vitest suite 145 → **147 passing across 14 spec files**. **MAJORs carried to P2-4b backlog per reviewer's gate decision**: salary scale assignment stub (`hr_employee_positions.salary_scale_id` — additive ALTER first commit in P2-4b); salary review per-department scope (Wave 2 Phase 2 role-split work). CI parity green: format:check + lint:logs (563 files clean) + vitest 147/147 + API + web build all clean. Awaiting Round 2 verdict before tagging `p2c4a-complete`. **Phase 2 Cycle 2 (P2C2 Incident & Emergency, M91) — COMPLETE + APPROVED at the closeout commit (REVIEW-P2C2-CHATGPT — final verdict, 2026-05-09).** Round 2 against `e569099` returned **PASS** with one carry-forward MAJOR hardening item: `vis_emergency_muster` had no UNIQUE constraint on `(school_id, incident_id)`, leaving a narrow window where a `VisitorMusterConsumer` crash between INSERT commit and idempotency claim could allow a redelivered event to land a duplicate muster row for the same incident. Tagged `p2c2-complete` at `e569099` (the Round 1 fix that earned PASS) and `p2c2-approved` at the closeout commit. **Round 2 closeout fix:** **Migration `108_vis_muster_incident_uq.sql`** adds a partial UNIQUE INDEX `vis_muster_school_incident_uq ON vis_emergency_muster(school_id, incident_id) WHERE incident_id IS NOT NULL`. The partial WHERE preserves the legitimate stand-alone fire-drill use case (drill_type=FIRE_DRILL with incident_id NULL — the P2C1 demo seed has exactly one such row). Verified live with 4 schema assertions: two NULL incident_id rows coexist for the same school; first incident-linked accepted; duplicate (school, incident) rejected with `unique_violation`; same incident across two schools coexist (per-school scoping preserved). **`VisitorMusterConsumer.materialiseMuster`** rewritten to `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (school_id, incident_id) WHERE incident_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING ... RETURNING id`. When ON CONFLICT fires, RETURNING is empty → consumer logs `[visitor-muster] muster already exists for incident=... (idempotent no-op via ON CONFLICT)` and resolves successfully so `processWithIdempotency` claims the redelivery and the Kafka event drops out of the consumer-group queue. A real DB failure (FK violation, outage) still rethrows so the claim is not taken and the next redelivery retries. **4 new unit tests** in `apps/api/src/visitors/visitor-muster.consumer.spec.ts`: INSERT SQL contains the ON CONFLICT clause + partial WHERE predicate; RETURNING-empty resolves successfully (does not throw — load-bearing assertion since processWithIdempotency would otherwise loop forever on the same conflict); RETURNING-with-row resolves successfully; real DB failure rethrows. **Vitest 100 → 104 passing tests across 12 spec files.** CI parity: format:check + lint:logs (546 files clean, +1 for the new spec) + vitest 104/104 + API + web build all green. **Wave A (Pilot Critical) ships P2C2 clean — Phase 2 Wave A continues with the next cycle on the roadmap.** See `HANDOFF-P2C2.md` "REVIEW-P2C2 ROUND 2 — closeout (PASS verdict)" section for the per-fix verification trail.

The Cycle 7 TaskWorker subscribes to this topic and creates an URGENT 72-hour escalating task. **A missed 72-hour window is a regulatory violation** — this is the highest-urgency automated escalation in CampusOS. Verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-07: smoke breach created with `notificationDeadline=2026-05-10T12:31:35` (= discovery + 72h) and full ADR-057 envelope captured on `dev.dpo.breach.discovered`. (2) **DPIA + DPA COMPLIANCE GAP DETECTION** — two schema-level partial INDEXes back the dashboard gap rules: `dpo_pa_high_risk_no_dpia_idx ON (school_id) WHERE high_risk_processing=true AND dpia_id IS NULL` for the DPIA gap; `dpo_proc_dpa_gap_idx ON (school_id) WHERE dpa_in_place=false` for the DPA gap. Both surface as red rows on the ROPA / processor registers + as gap-count cards on the unified `/governance` dashboard. Verified live: dashboard returns dpiaGaps=1 (AI Tutor without DPIA), dpaGaps=2 (OpenAI no DPA + Google expired). (3) **30/45-DAY SAR DEADLINE TRACKING** — `dpo_subject_access_requests.deadline_date` is computed from `dpo_compliance_dashboard_config.sar_default_deadline_days` (30 days GDPR default; 45 days FERPA when applicable). Status flips RECEIVED → IN*PROGRESS / EXTENSION_REQUESTED → COMPLETED / DENIED / OVERDUE. Multi-column `completed_chk` keeps `completed_at` populated only for terminal states. (4) **AUDIT LOG FIELD-LEVEL PSEUDONYMISATION (ADR-052 KEYSTONE)** — `ErasureService.pseudonymiseAuditLog(actor, erasureId, {targetTable: 'platform_audit_log', targetField: 'metadata'})` runs cross-schema: rewrites `platform.platform_audit_log.metadata` JSONB for rows where `actor_id = data_subject_id OR (entity_type='iam_person' AND entity_id=data_subject_id)`, replacing with `{"pseudonymised": "<token>"}` where token is `psd*<16-hex>`. Then INSERTs one row into `dpo*pseudonymisation_log`with`(target_table, target_field, rows_pseudonymised, pseudonymisation_token, pseudonymised_by)`. The first surface in CampusOS that mutates `platform.platform_audit_log`from a tenant-scoped service. (5) **AGE-18 RIGHTS TRANSFER** —`platform.platform_students.data_subject_is_self`boolean flips`false → true`when the student turns 18. SarService refuses parent-submitted requests after the flip with`"This student is the data subject for their own data (age 18+). Only the student or a DPO administrator can submit a SAR for their data."`Pre-existing parent-submitted SARs continue to process per their original deadline. (6) **IMMUTABLE PSEUDONYMISATION LOG** —`dpo_pseudonymisation_log`is append-only at the service layer (no UPDATE / no DELETE methods exposed). Mirrors Cycle 8`tkt_ticket_activity`+ Cycle 10`hlth_health_access_log`+ Cycle 11`svc_referral_activity`. NO ACTION FK to `dpo_erasure_requests`so the audit chain survives even if the erasure request is later removed (which it cannot be via the API). **Backend module**: GovernanceModule with **10 services + 1 controller + 49 endpoints** under`dpo-001:read/write/admin`(ROPA + retention + DPIA) +`dpo-002:read/write/admin`(processors + DPAs) +`dpo-003:read/write/admin`(breach management) +`dpo-004:read/write/admin`(SARs + erasure) +`dpo-005:read/write/admin` (consent + privacy notices) + 1 Kafka emit topic (`dpo.breach.discovered`). Services across `ropa.service.ts`(RopaService — processing activities + retention policies CRUD with DPIA gap tagging + retention review-due flag),`dpia.service.ts`(DpiaService — DPIA lifecycle SCOPING → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED → APPROVED/REJECTED with terminal-status guards),`processors.service.ts`(ProcessorService — processors + DPAs CRUD with atomic dpa_in_place backlink),`breach.service.ts`(**BreachService — THE 72-HOUR COUNTDOWN KEYSTONE**),`sar.service.ts`(**SarService — AGE-18 RIGHTS TRANSFER KEYSTONE** with three-persona row scope: DPO-internal sees all; GUARDIAN sees own-submitted + own-children's via sis_student_guardians + sis_guardians join; STUDENT sees own; nobody else),`erasure.service.ts`(**ErasureService — AUDIT LOG PSEUDONYMISATION KEYSTONE** + ConsentService + PrivacyNoticeService + ComplianceConfigService). **Step 4 seed**:`seed-dpo.ts`(idempotent, gated on whether`dpo_processing_activities`is already populated for the demo school) — 5 processing activities (1 high_risk no DPIA = the AI Tutor gap row), 3 retention policies (Academic 7y FERPA / Health 25y / CCTV 30d), 1 DPIA (Biometric Attendance APPROVED with residual=LOW), 4 third-party processors (AWS active + DPA / Stripe active + DPA / OpenAI no DPA = gap / Google expired DPA = gap), 2 DPAs ACTIVE, 1 data breach record (Stolen Laptop, THEFT, HIGH, 18h-elapsed at seed time, 54h remaining), 1 SAR (David Chen for Maya, IN_PROGRESS, deadline +25d), 1 erasure request (PARTIALLY_COMPLETED with academic retained + audit pseudonymised), 1 IMMUTABLE pseudonymisation log entry, 3 consent records (2 active CONSENTED + 1 WITHDRAWN), 1 privacy notice v2.1 PUBLISHED, 1 compliance dashboard config (SAR 30d default, breach escalation 70h). Wired as`seed:dpo`. **`seed-iam.ts`extended**: Parent gains`DPO-004:read+write`(47 perms total, +2 — SAR self-service for own children); Student gains`DPO-004:read+write`(52 perms, +2 — own SAR submission post-age-18); Staff (covers DPO stand-in) gains`DPO-001..005:read+write`(168 perms, +10); School Admin / Platform Admin retain admin-tier on all 5 DPO codes via`everyFunction`(495 each, +15). Catalogue 480 → **495 permissions = 165 functions × 3 tiers** (+15 DPO codes). **Note on parent erasure scope:** parent holds`dpo-004:write`for SAR self-service, but`ErasureService.hasDpoScope`and`SarService.hasDpoScope`(mutation path) tighten to also require`personType === 'STAFF'`so a parent cannot read the erasure register or mutate any SAR's status — those are DPO-internal. Verified live: parent /governance/erasures → 403; parent POST /governance/sars (own children) → 201. **Web side**: new`Data Governance`launchpad tile gated on`dpo-001:read`using new`ShieldIcon`. **11 web routes**: `/governance`(compliance command-centre with 8-stat header + 72-hour breach countdown panel + overdue SARs panel + module nav chips),`/governance/processing-activities`(ROPA list with DPIA gap chip filter),`/governance/processing-activities/[id]`(activity detail with inlined linked DPIA card showing residual risk + risks identified),`/governance/retention`(retention policies with review-due chip filter),`/governance/processors`(processor register with DPA gap chip filter + transfer mechanism column),`/governance/breaches`(register with pending-notification chip filter + per-row 72h countdown badge colour-coded green ≥36h / amber 12-36h / red ≤12h or overdue + risk pill + status pill),`/governance/breaches/[id]`(detail with structured sections + admin Notify-supervisory-authority Modal capturing reference number + Mark-resolved button with confirm),`/governance/sars`(queue with 6 status filter chips + days-until-deadline column with overdue-row tinting),`/governance/erasures`(request list with categories chip triplet + admin **Pseudonymise audit log button** opening confirm + IMMUTABLE pseudonymisation log table below),`/governance/consents`(consent ledger with active-only chip filter + state pills),`/governance/privacy-notices`(version timeline with Current pill + supersession dates). New`apps/web/src/lib/governance-format.ts`(per-status pill maps for SAR/erasure/breach/DPIA/DPA +`formatBreachCountdown`returning`{label, tone}`) + `apps/web/src/hooks/use-governance.ts`with 20 React Query hooks + 9 mutations. **Vertical-slice CAT** at`docs/cycle30-cat-script.md`walks 10 plan scenarios end-to-end (S1 6 permission denial paths; S2 SAR row scope; S3 dashboard rollup all 15 stats verified; S4 ROPA gap returns 1 (AI Tutor); S5 processor DPA gap returns 2 (OpenAI + Google); S6 seeded breach countdown 18h since/53h remaining; **S7 KEYSTONE** breach create +`dpo.breach.discovered`envelope captured live with`notificationDeadline = discovery + 72h`; S8 SA notification flips status UNDER_INVESTIGATION → NOTIFIED; S9 parent self-service SAR submission with guardian-link gate enforced; **S10 KEYSTONE** audit log pseudonymisation writes IMMUTABLE log row with opaque token `psd*<16hex>`). **Splitter trap caught + fixed pre-provision**: migration 098 had 1 stray `;`in block-comment description (rewritten as em-dash); migration 099 had 1 stray`;`in COMMENT ON TABLE string (rewritten as period); migration 100 splitter audit clean on first try. **Cycle 29 (Analytics & Reporting) — original Round 1 build state.** All 10 steps shipped + vertical-slice CAT verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-07. **Cycle 29 ships the M110 Analytics module — 16 of the 34 ERD tables in scope across 3 migrations (095 + 096 + 097)**. The operational read layer per ADR-008 CQRS-lite. **Wave 7 (Analytics & Governance) opens here** (Cycle 30 closes the wave). **Six structural keystones**: (1) **READ MODEL OWNERSHIP (ADR-008)** — every `rpt_*` table has exactly one owning module + one writing worker; the Analytics API surface is read-only on every `rpt_*` table; workers are the sole writers. (2) **FROM_SNAPSHOT REBUILD (ADR-049)** — `rpt_rebuild_snapshots` stores frozen aggregate state + per-topic-partition Kafka offsets; rebuild starts from snapshot + replays from offsets, never from beginning. (3) **OFFSET-BASED CHECKPOINTS** — `rpt_analytics_worker_checkpoints` stores `(consumer_group, topic, partition, committed_offset, log_end_offset, lag)`, never timestamps. (4) **CONFIGURABLE AT-RISK DETECTION** — `rpt_at_risk_configurations.trigger_conditions JSONB` lets schools express custom rules; `AtRiskEvaluationWorker` evaluates against `rpt_student_academic_summary` and emits `rpt.at_risk.flagged` for newly-flagged students. (5) **CHAINED NIGHTLY EXECUTION** — SIS → Classroom → AtRisk → SchoolSummary → District (03:00 UTC) → Wellbeing → Finance, the most complex background pipeline in CampusOS. Each worker is independent + idempotent. (6) **REPORT ENGINE WITH CRON SCHEDULING** — `rpt_scheduled_reports` carries cron expression + timezone + recipient list; **first cron-driven worker in CampusOS**. **Backend module**: AnalyticsModule with **7 workers + 3 services + 1 controller + 30 endpoints + 1 Kafka emit topic** (`rpt.at_risk.flagged`). Workers: SISReadModelWorker, ClassroomReadModelWorker, AtRiskEvaluationWorker, SchoolSummaryWorker, DistrictAnalyticsWorker, WellbeingTrendsWorker, FinanceARWorker, ScheduledReportWorker. **Cycle 28 (School Store) — original Round 1 build state.** All 10 steps shipped + vertical-slice CAT verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06. **Cycle 28 ships the M67 School Store module — 9 new tenant `str_*` base tables across 3 migrations (092 + 093 + 094).** Tenant logical base table count 362 → **371**. **13 intra-tenant FKs** (CASCADE × 7 + NO ACTION × 4 + SET NULL × 2). 0 cross-schema FKs — every cross-module ref is soft per ADR-001/020. **Wave 6 (Finance & Commerce) closes here** (Cycle 26 opened with Finance; Cycle 27 added Procurement; Cycle 28 closes with the School Store). **Five structural keystones**: (1) **PARENT APPROVAL GATE (ADR-062 KEYSTONE)** — every STUDENT-type order auto-creates a `str_order_approvals` row with `status='PENDING'` inside the same tenant tx as the order INSERT. Inventory is reserved (`quantity_reserved += quantities`) but `quantity_on_hand` is untouched until fulfilment. Payment is NOT charged. On parent approve: order flips PENDING*APPROVAL → PROCESSING + payment=CHARGED + `str.order.completed` emits AFTER tx commit. On parent decline: order flips PENDING_APPROVAL → CANCELLED + reservation released atomically. Multi-column `responded_chk` lockstep + UNIQUE(order_id) enforce the contract at the schema layer. Verified live: Maya places Calculator order → David approves → order=PROCESSING + payment=CHARGED + envelope on the wire; second order with decline → CANCELLED + reservation released back from 1 to 0. (2) **DUAL-MODE STORE** — `str_stores.store_type` is a 2-value CHECK (STUDENT, PUBLIC) with UNIQUE(school_id, store_type). STUDENT mode flows through the parent approval gate; PUBLIC mode uses `external_customer_id` instead of `customer_person_id`, requires `shipping_method=SHIPPED` with `shipping_option_id`, and skips the gate entirely. Three multi-column shape CHECKs (`customer_shape_chk`, `student_shape_chk`, `shipping_shape_chk`) on `str_orders` enforce the contract at the schema layer. (3) **CROSS-MODULE TO Cycle 6 PAYMENTS (Wave 1 ↔ Wave 6 KEYSTONE)** — `str.order.completed` envelope fires AFTER tx commit with payload `{orderId, schoolId, storeId, orderType, customerPersonId, externalCustomerId, total, lineItems: [{productId, quantity, unitPrice, lineTotal}], paymentMode}` so Cycle 6 M84 Family Billing can charge the matching `pay_family_account` (STUDENT/PARENT) or stub the external charge (EXTERNAL). The store never writes to `pay*_`tables directly per ADR-001/020. The Cycle 6 consumer is Phase 2 work; this cycle ships the emit + verified envelope on the wire. (4) **CROSS-MODULE TO Cycle 27 PROCUREMENT** —`str.inventory.reorder_needed`envelope fires when`quantity_on_hand`crosses to`<= reorder_point`, with payload `{productId, schoolId, productName, sku, currentStock, reorderPoint, reorderQuantity, preferredSupplierId}`for the future Cycle 27 procurement consumer to auto-create a`prc_requisitions`row pre-filled with the line. Delta-based dedup — fires only on the boundary crossing. Verified live: PE Kit adjusted from 30 → 5 (the seeded reorder_point) → envelope captured on`dev.str.inventory.reorder_needed`with currentStock=5 reorderPoint=5. (5) **REVENUE MATERIALISATION (ADR-018)** —`str_store_revenue`is a periodic materialised read model maintained by`RevenueService.materialise(storeId, periodStart, periodEnd)`which aggregates COMPLETED orders into`total_orders + total_revenue + total_cost + gross_margin`and UPSERTs on`(store_id, period_start, period_end)`so re-runs are idempotent. **Backend module**: StoreModule with **6 services + 1 controller + ~26 endpoints + 1 public endpoint** under`str-001:read/write/admin`(Stores + Products + Inventory) +`str-002:read/write/admin`(Orders + Approvals) +`str-003:read/write/admin` (External Customers + Shipping + Revenue) + 2 Kafka emit topics (`str.order.completed`, `str.inventory.reorder_needed`). 0 new Kafka consumers — Store is a pure emitter into the cross-module event bus this cycle. **Step 4 seed**: `seed-store.ts`(idempotent, gated on whether`str_stores` already exists) — 2 stores ("Lincoln Academy Shop" STUDENT + "Eagle Merchandise" PUBLIC), 6 products (School Polo $25, PE Kit $35 reorder_point=5, Yearbook 2026 $20, Scientific Calculator $15 backorder_allowed=true, Eagle Hoodie $45, Alumni Mug $12), 6 inventory rows, 2 historical orders (Maya STUDENT order COMPLETED + Jane Smith EXTERNAL order SHIPPED), 1 historical APPROVED approval (David Chen approved), 1 external customer (Jane Smith), 2 shipping options (Standard 5-7 days $5 + Express 2-3 days $15), 1 historical revenue snapshot (April 2026: 1 order, $45 revenue). **`seed-iam.ts`extended**: Teacher gains`STR-001:read`(86 perms total, +1 — browse catalogue); Parent gains`STR-001:read + STR-002:read+write`(45 perms total, +3 — browse + place orders for own children + approve/decline child orders); Student gains`STR-001:read + STR-002:read+write`(50 perms total, +3 — browse + place own orders); Staff gains`STR-001..003:read+write`(152 perms total, +6 — store manager stand-in until role split lands). School Admin / Platform Admin retain admin-tier on all 3 STR codes via`everyFunction`. Catalogue 465 → **468** (+1 function `STR-003`"External Customers, Shipping & Revenue" added in Step 4 to scope External Customers + Shipping + Revenue separately from Stores/Products and Orders/Approvals). **Web side**: new`Store`launchpad tile gated on`str-001:read`using new`ShoppingBagIcon`; persona-aware copy. **8 web routes**: 7 under `/store/_` (`/store`persona-aware home with stat cards (open orders, pending approvals, low stock) + catalogue chips + my orders;`/store/checkout`student checkout with parent-approval banner + cart;`/store/admin/products`admin product CRUD with modal;`/store/admin/orders`fulfilment queue with mark-ready / ship / complete / cancel actions;`/store/admin/inventory`inventory dashboard with adjust modal + amber tinting at-or-below reorder;`/store/admin/revenue`revenue summary with materialise modal;`/store/approvals` parent approval portal with approve/decline modal + decline reason) + 1 unauthenticated public storefront route at the app root (`/shop/[storeId]`). Both`tenant_demo`and`tenant_test`provisioned cleanly. **6 reviewer attention items** carried to Phase 2 punch list (joining items already on the broader Wave 2/6 backlog): (1) public storefront order placement — Stripe Checkout integration deferred; (2) Cycle 6 family-billing consumer for`str.order.completed`; (3) Cycle 27 procurement consumer for `str.inventory.reorder_needed`; (4) Store Manager role split (joins items 9 / 11 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 22 / 25 / 26 / 30 / 32); (5) reorder emit on the order-completion path (currently fires only via explicit admin adjust); (6) persistent shopping cart + product variants + discount codes + bundles + backorder lifecycle UX. **Cycle 27 (Procurement) — original Round 1 build state.** All 10 steps shipped + vertical-slice CAT verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06. **Cycle 27 ships the M86 Procurement module — 12 new tenant `prc_*` base tables across 3 migrations (089 + 090 + 091).** Tenant logical base table count 350 → **362**. **14 intra-tenant FKs** (CASCADE × 4 + NO ACTION × 9 + DB-enforced FK × 1 to `fin_suppliers`). 0 cross-schema FKs — every cross-module ref is soft per ADR-001/020 except the Cycle 26 `fin_suppliers(id)` FK on `prc_purchase_orders.vendor_id` and `prc_vendor_performance.vendor_id`. **Wave 6 (Finance & Commerce) continuation cycle** (Cycle 26 opened Wave 6 with Finance; Cycle 28 closes with the School Store). The Procurement Officer / Purchasing Clerk is the **eleventh specialist operator persona** after the nurse, counsellor, librarian, athletic director, enrolment officer, transportation coordinator, food service manager, facilities manager, IT administrator, and CFO/Business Manager. **Three structural keystones**: (1) **BUDGET COMMITMENT (Cycle 26 ↔ Cycle 27 KEYSTONE)** — `PurchaseOrderService.transition({action:'ISSUE'})` opens `executeInTenantTransaction`, locks the PO row + parent `fin_budget_lines` row `FOR UPDATE`, validates remaining budget, INSERTs `prc_budget_commitments` (status=COMMITTED, committed_amount=PO total), increments `fin_budget_lines.encumbered_amount` by the PO total, and flips the PO to ISSUED + parent requisition to ORDERED — all inside one tenant tx. CLOSE / CANCEL release the commitment + decrement encumbered_amount in the same atomic shape. The Cycle 26 budget-vs-actual variance dashboard immediately reflects every commit/release. Verified live: PO total $3,250 → encumbered_amount += $3,250 atomically; close → encumbered_amount drops back. (2) **CROSS-MODULE DISTRIBUTION (Wave 1 ↔ Wave 2 ↔ Wave 4 ↔ Wave 6 KEYSTONE)** — `DistributionService.create()` writes `prc_distributions` + `prc_distribution_lines` rows then emits `prc.distribution.completed` AFTER tx commits with payload `{distributionId, receiptId, purchaseOrderId, schoolId, destinationModule, destinationDepartment, distributedAt, sourceRefId, lines: [{receiptLineId, itemDescription, quantity, unitCost}]}`. 8 destination modules each have a `destination_module` token: `tech` (Cycle 22 IT), `trn` (Cycle 19 Transportation), `fds` (Cycle 20 Food Service), `lib` (Cycle 12 Library), `ath` (Cycle 13 Athletics), `ext` (Cycle 17 Clubs), `fac` (Cycle 21 Facilities), `str` (Cycle 28 School Store). Each module's inventory worker (Phase 2) consumes the event and creates the appropriate inventory record. **Procurement never writes directly to another module's tables** per ADR-061. (3) **VENDOR PERFORMANCE AUTO-SCORING** — `GoodsReceiptService.create()` updates `prc_vendor_performance` atomically inside the same tenant tx as the receipt write — `total_orders` increments by 1, `accepted_count` += sum(quantity_accepted), `rejected_count` += sum(quantity_rejected), `on_time_deliveries` increments when `today <= expected_delivery_date`. `average_quality_score` recomputes as `accepted / (accepted + rejected)`; `average_delivery_score` as `on_time / total_orders`. Schools see vendor scorecards live without a nightly batch job. Same tx also auto-flips PO status to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED or RECEIVED based on cumulative line quantities. **Backend module**: ProcurementModule with **7 services + 1 controller + 28 endpoints** under `prc-001:read/write/admin` (Requisitions) + `prc-002:read/write/admin` (Purchase Orders + Receiving) + `prc-003:read/write/admin` (Distribution + Returns + Vendor) + 2 Kafka emit topics (`prc.requisition.submitted` + `prc.distribution.completed`). RequisitionService implements full lifecycle: row-scoped list (non-officer sees own only with collapsed 404 don't-leak-existence), DRAFT → SUBMITTED → DEPT_APPROVED → ADMIN_APPROVED → DISTRICT_APPROVED → ORDERED → RECEIVED → DISTRIBUTED → CLOSED state machine; submit emits Kafka envelope OUTSIDE the tx. PurchaseOrderService implements `create` (locks settings row `FOR UPDATE` to allocate next `po_number` from sequence; validates vendor active), `transition` (the BUDGET COMMITMENT KEYSTONE). GoodsReceiptService implements `create` (validates each po_line + remaining quantity; UPSERTs vendor_performance; auto-flips PO status). DistributionService implements `create` (the CROSS-MODULE KEYSTONE). ReturnService implements full SHIP/RESOLVE/CANCEL state machine with multi-column `prc_ret_resolved_chk` lockstep enforcement. VendorPerformanceService is read-only. ProcurementSettingsService auto-creates default settings on first read; admin-only update. **Step 4 seed**: `seed-procurement.ts` (idempotent, gated on `prc_procurement_settings`) — 1 settings row, 2 requisitions + 5 lines, 1 PO PO-2026-001 with 2 lines (RECEIVED), 1 receipt with 2 lines (9 GOOD + 1 DAMAGED, ACCEPTED_WITH_DISCREPANCY), 1 budget commitment $3,250 against `account_code='5000'` Supplies budget line + bumps `fin_budget_lines.encumbered_amount` by $3,250, 1 distribution + 2 distribution lines (9 Chromebooks → tech/IT Asset Pool), 1 WARRANTY_CLAIM return INITIATED, 1 vendor performance row for Dell Education (totalOrders=1, on_time=1, accepted=9, rejected=1, quality=0.9, delivery=1.0). Wired as `seed:procurement`. **`seed-iam.ts` extended**: Teacher gains `PRC-001:read+write` (85 perms total, +2 for self-service requisitioning); Staff gains `PRC-001..003:read+write` (146 perms total, +6 — the Procurement Officer stand-in). School Admin / Platform Admin retain admin-tier on all 3 PRC codes via `everyFunction`. Catalogue stays at 465 — `PRC-001..003` already in catalogue from Wave 1. **Web side**: new `Procurement` launchpad tile gated on `prc-001:read` using new `ShoppingCartIcon`; persona-aware copy. **13 web routes**: `/procurement` (persona-aware dashboard with 4-stat header + nav chips + recent reqs + open POs + open returns); `/procurement/requisitions` + `/new` + `/[id]` (filterable list, create form with line-item editor, detail with status transitions + action bar); `/procurement/purchase-orders` + `/new` + `/[id]` (filterable list, create form with `?requisitionId=` pre-populate, **detail with BUDGET COMMITMENT KEYSTONE Issue Modal** that warns about the commitment); `/procurement/receiving` (PO picker + per-line receive form with quantity-balance validation); `/procurement/distribution` (PO + Receipt picker + accepted-lines table + **CROSS-MODULE KEYSTONE Modal** with destination module dropdown); `/procurement/receipts/[id]?poId=…` (receipt detail with returns + distributions); `/procurement/returns` (filterable global list with per-row Mark-shipped + Resolve Modal + Cancel); `/procurement/vendors` (vendor performance scorecards with green/amber/rose pill thresholds); `/procurement/commitments` (active budget commitments with total active encumbrance stat). New `apps/web/src/lib/procurement-format.ts` + `apps/web/src/hooks/use-procurement.ts` with 18 React Query hooks. **Vertical-slice CAT** at `docs/cycle27-cat-script.md` walks 10 plan scenarios end-to-end (S1 teacher submits requisition + Kafka envelope on `dev.prc.requisition.submitted`; S2 multi-level approval chain; **S3 BUDGET COMMITMENT KEYSTONE** Issue PO → encumbered_amount bumped atomically; S4 receive goods with 1 damaged → vendor performance auto-updated + PO auto-flips to RECEIVED; **S5 CROSS-MODULE DISTRIBUTION KEYSTONE** → `prc.distribution.completed` envelope on the wire with `destination_module="tech"`; S6 initiate damaged return + ship + resolve as REPLACED; S7 close PO releases the commitment atomically; S8 5 permission denial paths; S9 settings auto-create + admin-only update; S10 reject path). **Splitter trap caught + fixed pre-provision**: migration 090 had 2 stray `;` instances (1 in block-comment header rewritten with comma + 1 inside COMMENT string rewritten as em-dash); 091 had 1 stray `;` in a COMMENT string (rewritten with "and" / ", "); 089 clean on first audit. **Cycle 26 (Finance & Accounting) — original Round 1 build state.** All 10 steps shipped + vertical-slice CAT verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06. **Cycle 26 ships the M83 Finance & Accounting module — 14 new tenant `fin_*` base tables across 3 migrations (086 + 087 + 088).** Tenant logical base table count 336 → **350**. **17 intra-tenant FKs** (CASCADE × 5 + NO ACTION × 12); 0 cross-schema FKs. **Three structural keystones**: (1) **DOUBLE-ENTRY BALANCE VALIDATION (ADR-058/ADR-059 KEYSTONE)** — `PostingService.post(id)` runs `SUM(debit) = SUM(credit) AND COUNT(*) > 0` validation inside the same `executeInTenantTransaction` callback as the status flip to POSTED. On imbalance the entire transaction rolls back. The validation lives in service code rather than as a DB stored function because `provision-tenant.ts` splits on every `;` without dollar-quote awareness — a CREATE FUNCTION block whose body uses statement terminators would be cut mid-body. The integrity guarantee is identical because both paths execute under one transaction and rely on Postgres rollback semantics. Verified live: balanced batch (debit 500 / credit 500) → POSTED 200; unbalanced (debit 500 / credit 400) → 400 pre-flight rejection. (2) **PERMANENT PERIOD LOCK** — `fin_accounting_periods.status` lifecycle FUTURE → OPEN → CLOSED → LOCKED. **`PeriodService.patchStatus` refuses any transition out of LOCKED** with the message "LOCKED periods are permanent and cannot transition to any other status. This is a financial integrity invariant." regardless of caller (not even Platform Admin override). The `PostingService.post` and `createAndPost` paths refuse any batch targeting a CLOSED or LOCKED period. Verified live: July 2025 LOCKED → attempt to revert to OPEN returns the canonical message; DRAFT batch targeting LOCKED period → POST returns "Cannot post to a LOCKED period." (3) **CROSS-CYCLE GL CONSUMER (Wave 1 → Wave 6 integration)** — `GLConsumer` subscribes to 5 `dev.pay.*` topics from Cycle 6 (M84 Family Billing) under group `gl-consumer`. Per inbound event: resolves the chart of accounts mapping (Cash 1000 + AR 1100 + Tuition 4000 + GENERAL fund), constructs a balanced journal batch per topic (`pay.payment.received` → DEBIT Cash + CREDIT Tuition; `pay.invoice.created` → DEBIT AR + CREDIT Tuition; `pay.refund.issued` → DEBIT Tuition + CREDIT Cash), calls `PostingService.createAndPost(...)` with the Kafka `event_id` as `sourceEventId`. The `fin_journal_batches.source_event_id UNIQUE` constraint provides Kafka redelivery idempotency — a redelivered event silently returns the existing batch. The first Kafka consumer in CampusOS that writes financial data. **Verified live end-to-end on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06**: parent pays $30 invoice via `/invoices/:id/pay` → Cycle 6 emits `pay.payment.received` → GLConsumer auto-posts AUTO-019DFF45 batch (DEBIT Cash $30 / CREDIT Tuition $30) — POSTED with source_module='payments' + source_event_id populated; consumer log line `[gl-consumer] posted batch AUTO-019DFF45 (019dff45) from pay.payment.received eventId=019dff45` captured. **Backend module**: FinanceModule with **11 services + 1 controller + 36 endpoints** under `fin-005:read/write/admin` (General Ledger + Chart of Accounts + Periods) + `fin-006:read/write/admin` (Operating Budgets) + `fin-007:read/write/admin` (Accounts Payable) + `fin-008:read/write/admin` (Reconciliation, Board Reports & Grants) + 1 Kafka consumer (GLConsumer). **Step 4 seed**: `seed-finance.ts` (idempotent, gated on whether the GENERAL fund already exists) — 3 funds (GENERAL operating + TITLE_I SPECIAL_REVENUE + CAPITAL_PROJECTS), 15 chart of accounts (Assets 1000 Cash + 1100 AR + 1200 Prepaid; Liabilities 2000 AP + 2100 Accrued; Equity 3000 Fund Balance; Revenue 4000 Tuition + 4100 Fees + 4200 Grants; Expenses 5000 Supplies + 5100 Salaries + 5200 Utilities + 5300 Maintenance + 5400 Technology + 5500 Food Service; 1000/1100/2000 flagged `is_system=true`), 12 accounting periods covering FY2025-2026 (1 LOCKED + 2 CLOSED + 7 OPEN + 2 FUTURE), 2 POSTED journal batches with 4 balanced GL entries (Batch 1 AUTO_PAYMENT $3,500 tuition; Batch 2 MANUAL $1,200 supplies), 1 APPROVED budget GENERAL FY2025-2026 + 10 lines, 1 supplier "Office Supplies Inc" + 1 primary contact, 1 PAID AP voucher V-2025-0001 + 1 ap_payment linked to Batch 2 via `journal_batch_id`, 1 VARIANCE_FLAGGED reconciliation_run for October Cash, 1 board_report_snapshot BUDGET_VS_ACTUAL for September, 1 ACTIVE grant Title I Reading Improvement. Wired as `seed:finance`. **Permission catalogue: 454 → 465 codes** (4 new functions × 3 tiers — `FIN-005..008`). **`seed-iam.ts` extended**: Staff role gains `FIN-005..008:read+write` (140 perms total, +8 — the CFO stand-in); School Admin + Platform Admin pick up admin tier via `everyFunction` (465 perms each). Pre-existing `FIN-001..004` codes (Family Billing / Financial Aid / Fundraising / Budget Management) are NOT reused — `FIN-001:read+write` is held by parents from Cycle 6 family billing, so reusing it for the GL surface would leak finance access to parents at the gate. **Web side**: new `Finance` launchpad tile gated on `fin-005:read` (Staff + Admin only — intentionally invisible to parents/students/teachers) using new `CalculatorIcon`. **10 web routes**: `/finance` (CFO dashboard with 4-stat header + quick-nav chips + trial balance summary + period status pill grid + recent batches + variance-reconciliation alerts), `/finance/accounts` (chart grouped by 5 type sections with running balances + SYS+INACTIVE flags + admin includeInactive toggle), `/finance/journals` (status filter + per-batch View modal with the per-line debit/credit ledger + admin Post button on DRAFT triggering keystone validation + admin Void with required reason), `/finance/trial-balance` (full account table with totalDebit/totalCredit + Balanced/Imbalanced pill), `/finance/periods` (lifecycle table with admin transition buttons + **rose-tinted Lock confirmation modal with explicit "permanent and cannot be undone" warning matching the schema invariant**), `/finance/budgets` (per-fund variance dashboard with %used colour-coded amber >90% / rose >100%), `/finance/ap` (status filter + voucher table with overdue rose-tinting + admin Approve / Pay buttons; Pay modal triggers the cross-service keystone), `/finance/reconciliation`, `/finance/board-reports` (admin Generate + per-row View modal rendering the frozen JSONB snapshot + IMMUTABILITY notice), `/finance/grants` (per-grant cards with award/drawn progress bar). New `apps/web/src/lib/finance-format.ts` + `apps/web/src/hooks/use-finance.ts` with 20 React Query hooks. **Vertical-slice CAT** at `docs/cycle26-cat-script.md` walks 10 plan scenarios end-to-end (chart + funds + is_system protection / period lifecycle with LOCK irreversibility / **manual GL posting + balance validation keystone** / period LOCK refuses posting / **Kafka GL consumer cross-cycle keystone live-verified with parent-pays-$30 → AUTO-019DFF45 batch posted** / trial balance + budget variance / AP voucher lifecycle + journal_batch_id linkage / reconciliation VARIANCE_FLAGGED / 6 permission denial paths covering parent/student/teacher × 6 endpoints each). **Splitter trap caught + fixed pre-/mid-provision** — migration 087 had 1 stray `;` in a block comment (rewritten with periods) + 1 line-comment-before-CREATE-INDEX pattern that the splitter silently dropped (rewritten to use COMMENT ON INDEX after the CREATE); migration 088 had 10 stray `;` in a block comment header (rewritten with em-dashes); 086 clean on first audit. **MAJOR carry-overs to Phase 2 punch list**: (1) `validate_batch_balance` lives in the service layer rather than as a DB stored function — pre-pilot work is to extend the splitter to be dollar-quote-aware then move the validation into a DB function for defence in depth; (2) GLConsumer error path lacks DLQ alerting (joins item 8 from CLAUDE.md); (3) CFO role split joins items 9/11/13/14/16/22/25/26/30/32/33/34/35/36/37/38/39/40 in the broader role-split work; (4) seed period coverage vs runtime "today" — May 2026 ships FUTURE so the GLConsumer needs an OPEN period covering today, currently requires manual UPDATE; (5) dual finance permission families — pre-pilot rename FIN-001..004 → BIL-001..004 (Family Billing) and free up FIN-001..004 for the M83 General Ledger surface. Both `tenant_demo` and `tenant_test` provisioned cleanly. Plan at `docs/campusos-cycle26-implementation-plan.html`; handoff at `HANDOFF-CYCLE26.md`; CAT at `docs/cycle26-cat-script.md`. The Step 4 `StandardService.search` runs `to_tsvector(...) @@ plainto_tsquery(...)` against the platform catalogue with `ts_rank` ordering, plus a parallel ILIKE search on the smaller tenant catalogue, and returns unified results. The IT Administrator (IT admin) is the **ninth specialist operator persona** after the nurse, counsellor, librarian, athletic director, enrolment officer, transportation coordinator, food service manager, and facilities manager. **Closes Wave 4 (Campus Operations).** **Two structural keystones**: (1) **Encrypted Credential Vault per ADR-065 (SECURITY KEYSTONE)** — `tech_credential_vault` stores AES-256-GCM ciphertext + 16-byte auth tag (base64-encoded as `iv.tag.ciphertext`). The Step 6 `CredentialVaultService.getByIdWithPassword` resolves the actor's effective tier (STANDARD = baseline IT-005:read; ELEVATED = STAFF + IT-005:write; CRITICAL = School Admin OR IT-005:admin), refuses to decrypt when actor tier < credential tier, and writes a `VIEW` row to `tech_credential_access_log` inside the same tenant tx as the SELECT. Encryption key derived via `scryptSync` from `process.env.IT_VAULT_KEY` (separate from student-data key per ADR-065 — dev seed falls back to a deterministic seed string so seeded ciphertext decrypts cleanly through the same module). The access log is append-only at the service layer (no UPDATE / no DELETE methods exposed) per ADR-010 — mirrors Cycle 8 `tkt_ticket_activity` and Cycle 21 `fac_work_order_activity`. Verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06: principal (CRITICAL tier) decrypts seeded `School Wi-Fi Admin` (CRITICAL credential) → returns `password='SecureWifi-Admin-2026!'`; student (no IT-005:read) → 403 at controller gate. (2) **Software licence seat-utilisation auto-emit** — `LicenceService.assignSeat` locks the parent licence FOR UPDATE inside `executeInTenantTransaction`, validates seat capacity against multi-column `seats_chk` (`used_seats >= 0 AND used_seats <= total_seats when total_seats is set, total_seats > 0`), INSERTs `tech_software_assignments` (UNIQUE(licence_id, assignee_id)) + bumps `used_seats` in same tx, then emits `tech.licence.near_capacity` AFTER the tx commits when `used_seats / total_seats >= 0.80`. SITE licences (`total_seats=NULL`) skip the emit. Verified live: 5-seat S7 Smoke Pro licence assigned 5 times; ADR-057 envelope captured on `dev.tech.licence.near_capacity` with full shape (`event_type='tech.licence.near_capacity'`, `source_module='it'`, payload includes `licenceId / schoolId / softwareName / totalSeats=5 / usedSeats=5 / utilisationPct=100 / sourceRefId`). **Backend module**: ItModule with **12 services + 1 ItController + 52 endpoints** under `it-002:read/write/admin` (Device Fleet — assets / assignments / damage / repair / infrastructure / procurement) through `it-006:read/write/admin` (System Monitoring — MDM) + 1 Kafka emit topic. Services across `assets.service.ts` (AssetCategoryService + AssetService + AssignmentService + AssetDocumentService + DamageReportService + RepairRecordService — locked-row assign/return with multi-column `returned_chk` lockstep + condition tracking), `licences.service.ts` (LicenceService + CredentialVaultService — SECURITY KEYSTONE with AES-256-GCM via Node crypto), `mdm.service.ts` (MdmService + InfrastructureService + ProcurementService + DeviceSelectionService — ADR-066 parent-active onboarding workflow). **Step 4 seed**: `seed-it.ts` (idempotent, gated on `tech_asset_categories` row count) — 2 asset categories (Chromebook 4yr depreciation + iPad 3yr) + 10 assets (8 Chromebooks IT-CB-001..008 + 2 iPads IT-IP-001..002 across status mix: 8 ASSIGNED, 1 AVAILABLE, 1 REPAIR) + 8 active assignments + 2 warranty docs + 3 software licences (Google Workspace SITE / Adobe Creative Suite PER_SEAT 25 seats with 4 used / Zoom SUBSCRIPTION 100 seats) + 4 Adobe assignments + 2 vault entries (School Wi-Fi Admin CRITICAL + Google Console ELEVATED with deterministic AES-256-GCM ciphertext) + 2 access log entries + 5 infrastructure items (2 switches + 2 access points + 1 server) + 1 GOOGLE MDM sync + 1 STALE_CHECKIN alert on IT-CB-005 + 1 MODERATE damage report on IT-CB-007 + 1 WARRANTY_CLAIM IN_REPAIR repair record (FK to `tkt_vendors`) + 1 ORDERED procurement order (Q3 Chromebook Refresh, $3500, ordered_by=Mitchell as `hr_employees` FK) + 2 device options (Chromebook 14in standard + iPad 10th Gen premium) + 1 ENROLMENT-context SELECTED selection for Aiden Park. Wired as `seed:it`. **`seed-iam.ts` extended**: Teacher gains `IT-002:read+write + IT-003:read+write + IT-004:read` (73 perms total, +5 — own assigned device, damage reports, device selection during onboarding, view licences); Student gains `IT-002:read + IT-003:read+write` (40 perms, +3 — own devices visible, can SELECT during onboarding); Staff (covers IT admin) gains `IT-002..006:read+write` (122 perms, +10 — full asset/licence/vault/MDM/device-selection management; vault tier check at service layer prevents STANDARD-tier Staff from reading CRITICAL credentials); School Admin / Platform Admin retain admin-tier via `everyFunction` (453). **Cycle 21 (Facilities Management) — original Round 1 build state.** All 10 steps shipped + vertical-slice CAT verified live on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-06. The Facilities Manager (FM) is the **eighth specialist operator persona** after the nurse, counsellor, librarian, athletic director, enrolment officer, transportation coordinator, and food service manager. **Three structural keystones**: (1) **EXCLUDE gist booking conflict detection (KEYSTONE)** — `fac_space_bookings` carries `EXCLUDE USING gist (space_id WITH =, tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at) WITH &&) WHERE (status = 'CONFIRMED')` constraint preventing two CONFIRMED bookings on the same space with overlapping time windows from coexisting in the database. `BookingService.create` translates SQLSTATE 23P01 raised by the EXCLUDE into a friendly 409 Conflict response. **First schema-level temporal overlap prevention in CampusOS** outside the Cycle 5 timetable EXCLUSIONs. Live verified: first CONFIRMED 201, overlapping CONFIRMED 409, non-overlapping (back-to-back via `[)` half-open tstzrange) 201, status=CANCELLED drops out of the partial WHERE so a follow-up CONFIRMED at the same time succeeds. (2) **Immutable work order activity timeline** — `fac_work_order_activity` is append-only at the service layer (`WorkOrderService.recordActivityInTx` is the sole writer; no UPDATE / no DELETE methods exposed). Every status transition, reassignment, and comment writes a row inside the same tenant tx with `activity_type` (4-value CHECK STATUS_CHANGE/REASSIGNMENT/COMMENT/ATTACHMENT) + `metadata` JSONB. Mirrors Cycle 8 `tkt_ticket_activity`. Live verified: seeded REPAIR work order has 3 activity rows in chronological order (OPEN→IN_PROGRESS / COMMENT / IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED). When `MaintenanceTaskService.submitResults` writes a row with `passed=false`, it inserts a follow-up `fac_work_orders` row in the same tenant tx (status=OPEN, priority=MEDIUM, work_order_type=REPAIR, linked back via `follow_up_work_order_id`). (2) **No-show detection worker** — `NoShowService.runOnce()` walks expected ridership (`trn_student_assignments`) against actual scans (`trn_ridership_records`) and inserts `trn_no_show_alerts` ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (UNIQUE(student, route, expected_date, expected_stop) is the schema-side dedup gate) + emits `trn.no_show.detected`. Invalid / expired / inactive tokens return 400. **Pre-trip inspection FAIL safety gate**: `RunLogService.start` calls `assertVehicleInspectedAndPassing(vehicleId, runDate)` before stamping the run row; missing inspection → 400; FAIL → 400. Tenant base table count 239 → **247**. **9 intra-tenant FKs** (5 + 4); **0 cross-schema FKs**. **30 endpoints** under `grp-001:read/write/admin` across 5 services + 1 controller (GroupService + MembershipService + OwnershipTransferService + GroupAnnouncementService + GroupEventService). **2 new Kafka emit topics** (`grp.announcement.posted`, `grp.event.created`) — both ADR-057 envelopes captured live during the CAT. **1 new permission code** added to `permissions.json`: `GRP-001` (Groups & Communities, group="Communications"). Catalogue: 150 → **151 functions × 3 tiers = 453 permissions**. IAM Teacher / Student / Parent / Staff each gain `GRP-001:read+write`; Admin via everyFunction. Effective access cache rebuilt: admin 453 / teacher 64 / staff 82 / student 35 / parent 33. **Three structural keystones** verified end-to-end: (1) **two-party ownership transfer handshake** — partial UNIQUE(group_id) WHERE status='PENDING' caps pending transfers at one per group; `OwnershipTransferService.accept` opens a tenant transaction, locks the transfer + both grp_members rows with `FOR UPDATE`, demotes the from-member to ADMIN and promotes the to-member to OWNER, stamps `responded_at` per the multi-column `responded_chk` lockstep — all four updates inside one tx so a failure rolls back the entire handshake; live verified with the seeded Rivera→Mitchell PENDING transfer (Rivera as from-member 403 on accept; Mitchell accepts → Rivera ADMIN + Mitchell OWNER atomically). (2) **Scope-aware bindings** — `grp_groups.scope_type` is a 5-value CHECK (CLASS/YEAR_GROUP/SCHOOL/CUSTOM/ACTIVITY); multi-column `scope_pair_chk` enforces SCHOOL/CUSTOM with `scope_id IS NULL` and CLASS/YEAR_GROUP/ACTIVITY with `scope_id IS NOT NULL`; `GroupService.create` validates the supplied scope_id matches an existing row in the matching tenant table (`sis_classes` / `sis_academic_years` / `ext_activities`); Cycle 17's `ext_activities.group_id` soft FK closes the resolution loop in the other direction. (3) **Re-join semantics** — partial UNIQUE(group_id, person_id) WHERE status<>'LEFT' on `grp_members` caps active membership at one row but allows re-join after voluntary leave because LEFT rows drop out of the partial index; the multi-column `left_chk` keeps `left_at` populated only when status='LEFT'. **6-state member lifecycle** ACTIVE / INVITED / PENDING_APPROVAL / SUSPENDED / LEFT / REMOVED covers every transition the join-policy + admin-action matrix needs. **Web side**: new `Groups` launchpad tile gated on `grp-001:read` using `ChatBubbleIcon` with persona-aware copy; **4 new web routes** (`/groups` browse + create with scope filter chips + pending-transfer banner, `/groups/[id]` detail with 4 tabs Announcements / Events / Members / Transfers + Owner-only Transfer-ownership Modal + RSVP cap-aware buttons + read-receipt tracking, `/groups/my` aggregated active memberships, `/groups/feed` upcoming RSVPs). 25 React Query hooks in `use-groups.ts`. Wave 2 (Student Services & Enrichment) closes here.** **REVIEW-CYCLE13 fixes (2026-05-05):** (BLOCKING 1 — privacy) `InjuryService.list()` only restricted STUDENT actors; teachers + generic Staff with `ATH-004:read` could enumerate every athletic injury in the tenant. New private `buildVisibility(actor, nextParamPosition)` helper returns admin / AD = full access, STUDENT = own row only (resolved via `actor.personId → platform_students → sis_students`), STAFF + `employeeId` = students enrolled in classes they teach (`sis_class_teachers + sis_enrollments WHERE status='ACTIVE'`) UNION athletes on rosters where they have an active coaching assignment (`ath_coaching_assignments` keyed on `coach_person_id`), everyone else `[]`. The schema-side enrolment + coaching-assignment joins are the actual access boundary — the permission gate alone is not. (BLOCKING 2 — privacy) `GET /athletics/injuries/:id` returned the full DTO without actor-aware row scope and threw a raw `Error` for non-student callers. `InjuryService.getById(id, actor)` now applies the same `buildVisibility` predicate to the WHERE clause; non-authorised callers receive a collapsed `404 NotFoundException` rather than the row. Controller resolves the actor via `actors.resolveActor(...)` and passes it through; the post-fetch student check + raw `Error` throw are removed. (MAJOR 3 — concurrency) `RosterService.addMember()` cap-check + INSERT now wrap inside `executeInTenantTransaction` with `SELECT … FROM ath_rosters r … FOR UPDATE OF r` at the top of the tx so concurrent submissions serialise on the parent roster row; the cap re-check happens inside the same tx as the INSERT, so loser requests re-read the bumped count and 400. (MAJOR 4 — bug) `ResultService.patchResult()` previously updated the result row but never reversed / recomputed `ath_season_records`, so flipping outcome from WIN to LOSS would leave the record stale forever. `patchResult()` now refuses any `outcome` change with a friendly 400 redirecting the caller to the future reverse-and-re-enter correction workflow; score / `score_by_period` / notes corrections still pass because they do not affect the season-record aggregate. The locked-row reverse-and-recompute path is on the Phase 2 punch list. (MAJOR 5 — validation) `StatsService.bulkEnter()` resolves the parent game's `roster_id` inside the existing tenant tx and validates every supplied `studentId` against `ath_roster_members WHERE roster_id = $1 AND removed_at IS NULL AND student_id = ANY($2::uuid[])`; mismatches return a single 400 with the missing UUIDs inlined. The schema-side UNIQUE on `(game, student, category)` remains the dedup belt-and-braces. (MAJOR 7 — readability) `GameService.hasResultScope()` rewritten from a mixed sync/async `||` expression to explicit guard-style `if (actor.isSchoolAdmin) return true; if (await this.programmes.hasAdScope(actor)) return true; return …;`. Live verification (5 scenarios on `tenant_demo` 2026-05-05): teacher Rivera with no AD scope and no coaching assignment GETs /injuries → `[]` (was: every injury); GET /injuries/<seeded-id> → 404 (was: full DTO); after adding a coaching assignment for Rivera on Maya's roster, the same teacher sees Maya's injuries on the list endpoint and getById returns the DTO; 5 parallel POST /rosters/:id/members against a roster at cap-2-of-3 lands 1× 201 + 4× 400; PATCH result with `{outcome:'LOSS'}` against an existing WIN row returns 400 with the redirect message; POST /games/:id/stats with a non-roster studentId returns 400 with the offender UUIDs. LibraryModule now imports KafkaModule on top of TenantModule + IamModule. **`CheckoutService`** is the keystone — `checkout(input, actor)` resolves barcode → copy with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` to serialise concurrent scans, calls `resolvePatronType(personId)` (joins `platform.platform_students` first then `hr_employees` to determine STUDENT vs STAFF), reads the matching `lib_checkout_policies` row, validates `is_available=true` AND `count(active checkouts) < policy.maxCheckouts`, INSERTs the checkout row with `due_date = CURRENT_DATE + (policy.loanPeriodDays || ' days')::interval`, and UPDATEs the copy to `is_available=false / location_status='CHECKED_OUT'` all inside one tenant tx. **`returnCheckout(id, actor)` is the auto-fine + hold-reassignment keystone** — locks checkout row + computes `days_overdue = GREATEST(CURRENT_DATE - due_date, 0)::int`, stamps `returned_at + status='RETURNED'`, when `days_overdue > 0 AND policy.overdueFinePerDay > 0` INSERTs an OVERDUE fine (amount rounded to 2dp to dodge floating-point imprecision); then walks the hold queue with `SELECT … FROM lib_holds WHERE catalogue_item_id = $1 AND status='PENDING' ORDER BY placed_at ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE` — if a waiting hold exists, the hold flips to READY with `notified_at=now()` + the copy walks to `ON_HOLD_SHELF / is_available=false`; otherwise the copy returns to ON_SHELF. **`lib.fine.issued` emits AFTER the tx commits** so a Kafka hiccup can't roll back the patron's return; envelope payload includes `fineId / checkoutId / patronId / fineType / amount / daysOverdue / status='OUTSTANDING' / sourceRefId`. `renew(id, actor)` validates ACTIVE/OVERDUE + renewal_count < policy.renewalsAllowed, extends due_date, resets to ACTIVE so renewing an OVERDUE checkout clears the flag. **`HoldService`** — `placeHold(input, actor)` defaults `patronId` to `actor.personId` (self-service) with the `hasLibrarianScope` check guarding cross-patron placements; refuses duplicate PENDING/READY hold from same patron; validates parent item has at least one copy. `cancel(id, actor)` patron-or-librarian via service-layer row-scope. `collect(id, actor)` librarian-only, refused on non-READY status. **`FineService`** — `list` row-scopes patrons to own; AUTO worker writes`owner_id = assignee, created_for_id = NULL`; MANUAL self-task `owner_id = me, created_for_id = NULL`; MANUAL delegation `owner_id = assignee, created_for_id = me`(admin-only). The plan's auth note suggests the inverse but the schema and to-do-list mental model are clearer with this convention. **Acknowledge/dispute tx model:**`executeInTenantTransaction`with`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`on the ack row so two parallel calls serialise; validates subject_id match + PENDING status; UPDATEs ack + cascade-UPDATEs all linked`tsk_tasks`rows where status NOT IN (DONE, CANCELLED) to status='DONE' + completed_at=now() in the same UPDATE so the multi-column`completed_chk`is satisfied; Kafka emit outside the tx so a broker hiccup doesn't roll back the user's action. **Live verification on`tenant_demo`(23 scenarios all pass):** S1–S14 cover the 5 task endpoints + permission denials + delegation pathway with admin override; A1–A9 cover the 4 ack endpoints + the DONE-cascade verification + the row-scope 404 + the empty-reason 400 from class-validator + the ?all=true admin-only override. **Wire envelopes captured live with full ADR-057 shape:**`dev.task.completed`with`source_module:'tasks'`+ payload {taskId, ownerId, title, taskCategory, source:'MANUAL', sourceRefId:null, completedAt};`dev.student.acknowledgement.completed`with payload {acknowledgementId, subjectId, status:'ACKNOWLEDGED_WITH_DISPUTE', sourceType:'DISCIPLINE_RECORD', sourceRefId, disputeReason}. **Bug caught during smoke:** the first ack-smoke run keyed`subject_id`to the principal's`iam_person.id`instead of Maya's because the SQL JOIN reused the same`pu`row for both`subject_id`and`created_by`; Maya's GET returned 0 acks even though the rows existed.
