The TaskWorker is the **sole writer to `tsk_tasks`per ADR-011** — domain modules emit Kafka events, the worker translates them into rows. **Bootstrap:** reads`tsk_auto_task_rules`across every active school via`platform.schools`+`platform_tenant_routing`+`executeInExplicitSchema`, takes the union of distinct `trigger_event_type`values, env-prefixes via`prefixedTopic()`, and subscribes under group `task-worker`. Adding a new rule with a never-before-seen trigger type at runtime requires a worker restart — documented limitation. **Per-event flow:** `unwrapEnvelope`→`processWithIdempotency('task-worker', event)`claim-after-success → query active rules for this tenant + topic → AND-evaluate`tsk_auto_task_conditions`against payload (7-value operator enum EQUALS/NOT_EQUALS/IN/NOT_IN/GT/LT/EXISTS implemented in`evaluateCondition()`, JSON dot-paths for field_path) → resolve owners (`cls.assignment.posted`joins`sis_enrollments + sis_students + platform_students + platform_users`for the class;`target_role=SCHOOL_ADMIN`reads`platform.iam_effective_access_cache`with`'sch-001:admin' = ANY(permission_codes)`matching the`AbsenceRequestNotificationConsumer.loadSchoolAdminAccounts`precedent;`target_role=STUDENT`resolves a single account from`payload.studentId`; fallback reads `payload.recipientAccountId`) → execute actions in sort_order (`CREATE_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`inserts`tsk_acknowledgements`per owner returning a Map<owner, ack_id> for the next CREATE_TASK to link via`acknowledgement_id`; `CREATE_TASK`runs per-(owner, source_ref_id) Redis SET NX on`tsk:auto:{subdomain}:{owner}:{source_ref_id}`30-day TTL then INSERTs with`source='AUTO'`+ the rule's priority/category + rendered title + description, emits`task.created`with`correlation_id = inbound event_id`; `SEND_NOTIFICATION`reserved for future cycles). **Dedup is dual-layer:** per-event_id consumer-group claim catches Kafka redelivery of the same event row; per-(owner, source_ref_id) Redis SET NX catches "different event_id but same logical action" (a teacher PATCHing`isPublished=true`on an already-published assignment re-emits with a new event_id but the source_ref_id matches). The schema-level partial INDEX on`(owner_id, source, source_ref_id) WHERE source != 'MANUAL'`is non-unique (partitioned tables can't constrain across partitions without including the partition key) — investigation support only. **Three new helper additions**:`unprefixTopic(wireTopic)`in`apps/api/src/kafka/event-envelope.ts`(inverse of`prefixedTopic`so the worker matches wire topics back to logical`trigger_event_type`); `cls.assignment.posted`Kafka emit in`apps/api/src/classroom/assignment.service.ts`create + update paths whenever`is_published=true`lands (with`assignment_title`+`class_name`+`due_date`placeholders for the worker to render);`isPublished: true`field added to the`cls.grade.published`payload in`apps/api/src/classroom/grade.service.ts` so the seeded condition (`payload.isPublished = true`) actually evaluates against a present field — the topic name implies it but the field needs to be on the wire for the condition evaluator. **Live verification on `tenant_demo`2026-05-03:** pre-created the 8 trigger topics with`kafka-topics.sh --create --if-not-exists`(one-time dev workaround for the documented Cycle 3+5 subscribe-before-publish race); booted API; worker logged`TaskWorker subscribed to 8 topic(s)`cleanly; teacher Rivera POSTed an assignment "Step 4 Live Smoke — Photosynthesis Lab" with`isPublished:true`against P1 Algebra; within ~3s the worker created 1 row in`tsk_tasks`for Maya (the only ACTIVE enrollee) with`title='Complete: Step 4 Live Smoke — Photosynthesis Lab'`(rendered from`title_template='Complete: {assignment_title}'`), `owner_id`=student@, `source='AUTO'`, `source_ref_id`=assignment id, `priority='NORMAL'`, `task_category='ACADEMIC'`, `status='TODO'`; PATCHing the same assignment again with `isPublished:true`triggered the worker's dedup-hit log line`[task-worker] dedup hit on tsk:auto:demo:<owner>:<source_ref_id> — skipping task creation`and the task count stayed at 1; cleanup deleted the smoke task + smoke assignment + matching Redis dedup key. Out of scope this step (deferred): the remaining 7 auto-task rules are scaffolded but not exercised end-to-end yet — the keystone assignment.posted path verifies the engine and the smaller paths reuse the same resolveOwners / template-render / dedup machinery; runtime rule-add without worker restart; warmup-emit sweep at startup to dodge the topic-subscribe race. **Step 3 lands`packages/database/src/seed-tasks.ts`** **Step 3 lands `packages/database/src/seed-tasks.ts`** (idempotent, gated on `tsk_auto_task_rules`row count for the demo school) wired into`package.json`as`seed:tasks`. **Phase 2 Parent Polish landed 2026-05-03 (5 commits, no review yet).** Five separate commits between `44dff03` and `c9d2de7` ship cross-cutting improvements identified during parent testing — none of them tied to a numbered Cycle. (1) `44dff03` — iPhone-style dashboard launchpad: app tiles shrink from aspect-square cards to a 56×56 rounded icon box with a label below; hover tints the icon-box from campus-50 to campus-100; badge moves to `-right-1 -top-1` with `ring-2 ring-white` so it sits on top of the icon-box edge. Grid widens 4 cols mobile / 6 cols desktop. (2) `9f8658c` — calendar event RSVPs + my-children filter + multi-school selector. Tenant migration `023_sch_calendar_event_rsvps.sql` adds the RSVP table (3-value GOING/TENTATIVE/NOT_GOING CHECK, UNIQUE(event, person), soft FK to platform.iam_person). New `CalendarRsvpService` with 3 endpoints under `sch-003:read` — `POST /calendar/:id/rsvp` upserts, `GET /calendar/:id/rsvps` (admin all, others own), `GET /calendar/:id/rsvp-summary` aggregate counts + my response. `CalendarService.list` accepts an optional `myKidsPersonIds` array; controller resolves the parent's own personId plus children's personIds (via `StudentService.listForGuardianPerson`) when guardian + `myKidsOnly=true`. UI: guardian-only `My children only` toggle + multi-school selector dropdown (only renders for 2+ schools — placeholder for cross-tenant aggregation). Event detail Modal grows an RSVP panel with chip buttons + aggregate counts. Phase 3 carry-over: full audience targeting on calendar events (filter is RSVP-only today). (3) `adc78d4` — Add Child workflow with admin approval. Tenant migration `024_sis_child_link_requests.sql` with mutually exclusive LINK_EXISTING / ADD_NEW shapes (multi-column `shape_chk`) + PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED lifecycle (`reviewed_chk` keeps reviewer fields all-set or all-null). New `ChildLinkRequestService` with 6 endpoints under `/children` — search, link-request, add-request, list, approve, reject. `approve()` runs in `executeInTenantTransaction` with FOR UPDATE on the request row; ADD_NEW path atomically creates iam_person + platform_students + sis_students + sis_student_guardians + (when guardian has a household) platform_family_members CHILD entries. Emits `iam.child.linked`. UI: `/children` gains an Add child button with a 3-step Modal (SEARCH → PICK_RESULT → ADD_NEW); pending banner above the cards; new admin queue at `/children/link-requests` with status filter chips + per-row Approve/Reject Modal capturing reviewer notes. (4) `ae32299` — public enrollment search by location. Platform migration `20260503130749` adds `latitude` / `longitude` / `fullAddress` / `sharedBillingGroupId` (the last wired in commit 5) to `platform.schools`. Tenant migration `025_enr_period_allows_public_search.sql` adds `allows_public_search BOOLEAN DEFAULT true` to `enr_enrollment_periods` so existing OPEN periods auto-appear; invitation-only cycles flip false. New `EnrollmentSearchService` + `@Public()` `EnrollmentSearchController` at `GET /enrollment/search?lat=&lng=&radiusMiles=&gradeLevel=` (radius capped at 100 miles). Cross-tenant — phase 1 reads platform.schools + platform_tenant_routing then app-side Haversine filter; phase 2 enters each surviving tenant via the new `TenantPrismaService.executeInExplicitSchema(schemaName, fn)` helper. Two infra fixes the public endpoint surfaced: (a) `TenantGuard` is global so it ran on @Public() endpoints and threw on `getCurrentTenant()` — now reads `IS_PUBLIC_KEY` via `Reflector` and short-circuits, matching `AuthGuard`. (b) The middleware's exempt-path matcher used `req.path`, which Nest strips of the global `/api/v1` prefix before middleware runs — switched to `req.originalUrl` so the existing `/api/v1/health` entry actually matches (latent bug). Web: new `/find-schools` route at the app root (outside the auth-gated `(app)` layout) with lat/lng + "Use my location" button + radius slider + grade filter; login page gains a "Find a school accepting applications →" link below the account picker for unauth visitors. Verified live on `tenant_demo`: Springfield query finds Lincoln Elementary at 0.3 mi with the seeded Fall 2026 Admissions period; NYC query empty; grade=9 hits, grade=12 misses. (5) `c9d2de7` — multi-school billing structure. `family-account.service.ts` SELECT base joins `platform.schools` to surface `school_name` + `shared_billing_group_id` on every row; `FamilyAccountResponseDto` and the matching web `FamilyAccountDto` pick up the two new fields. Parent billing dashboard restructured to render one section per school, with sections grouped by `sharedBillingGroupId` when set (so two schools sharing a district billing module collapse into one combined section). Demo case (single tenant) shows one section with "Lincoln Elementary" header. Per-account UI extracted into `FamilyAccountSection.tsx` so the page is now a thin layout that maps over grouped accounts. Phase 3 carry-over: true cross-tenant aggregation (since tenancy is still per-request, this page only ever sees the current tenant's accounts). Schema impact: 2 new tenant tables (`sch_calendar_event_rsvps`, `sis_child_link_requests`) and 1 new tenant column on `enr_enrollment_periods` bring tenant base table count from 106 → **108**. 4 new platform columns on `platform.schools`. **HANDOFF-PHASE2-POLISH.md** carries the full per-feature detail; this list summarises what changed and where.

**Step 2 lands `016_sch_timetable_and_bookings.sql`** with 3 base tables on top of `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist` (the extension lives at database scope so it's idempotent across re-provisions and across multiple tenants on the same database): `sch_timetable_slots` (DB-enforced FKs to `sis_classes`, `sch_periods`, `sch_rooms`, and nullable `hr_employees` for TBD-teacher slots; `effective_from`/`effective_to` date range with NULL-end-date meaning open-ended; UNIQUE(class_id, period_id, effective_from); two `EXCLUDE USING gist` constraints — `sch_timetable_slots_teacher_no_overlap` and `sch_timetable_slots_room_no_overlap` — both shaped `(actor WITH =, period_id WITH =, daterange(effective_from, COALESCE(effective_to, 'infinity'::date), '[)') WITH &&)`). The half-open `[)` daterange means a slot ending on a date and another slot starting on the same date do **not** overlap — the natural rotation pattern. Open-ended slots coalesce NULL → infinity so they block every future date. `teacher_id` is nullable and the `=` operator class treats NULL-vs-NULL as not-equal, so two TBD-teacher slots on the same period and overlapping range do **not** conflict (the room EXCLUSION still catches the room collision). Constraint violations raise SQLSTATE 23P01 — Step 5's `TimetableService` will translate that to `409 Conflict`. `sch_room_bookings` (CONFIRMED/CANCELLED status with multi-column lifecycle CHECK that CANCELLED ⇒ cancelled_at NOT NULL, window CHECK end_at > start_at, partial INDEX on (room_id, start_at, end_at) WHERE CONFIRMED for the conflict-check hot path). `sch_room_change_requests` (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/AUTO_APPROVED with multi-column reviewed_chk that PENDING ⇔ reviewed_at NULL; nullable `requested_room_id` for the "any available" case; AUTO_APPROVED reserved for a future auto-approval sweep). 8 intra-tenant FKs (4 on sch_timetable_slots, 1 on sch_room_bookings, 3 on sch_room_change_requests), 0 cross-schema FKs. **Step 5 lands the first scheduling request-path module at `apps/api/src/scheduling/`** with 5 services + 5 controllers + 22 endpoints. `BellScheduleService` (6 endpoints: `GET /bell-schedules`, `GET /bell-schedules/:id`, `POST /bell-schedules` admin, `PATCH /bell-schedules/:id` admin, `POST /bell-schedules/:id/periods` admin (full upsert — DELETE all + INSERT each, atomic in one transaction so a UNIQUE / CHECK violation aborts the whole replacement instead of landing half-applied), `POST /bell-schedules/:id/set-default` admin (atomically clears any other default for the same school in the same tx so the partial UNIQUE INDEX never rejects the flip)). `TimetableService` (7 endpoints: `GET /timetable` with `classId` / `teacherId` / `roomId` / `onDate` filters, `GET /timetable/teacher/:employeeId`, `GET /timetable/class/:classId`, `GET /timetable/room/:roomId`, `POST /timetable/slots` admin, `PATCH /timetable/slots/:id` admin, `DELETE /timetable/slots/:id` admin) — every read joins through `sis_classes` + `sis_courses` for `classSectionCode` + `courseName`, `sch_periods` for `periodName` + `dayOfWeek` + `startTime` + `endTime`, `sch_rooms` for `roomName`, and LEFT JOINs `hr_employees` + `platform.iam_person` for `teacherName`. **The translateConflict helper is the load-bearing trick**: `INSERT` / `UPDATE` is wrapped in a try/catch; SQLSTATE 23P01 paired with the constraint name (`sch_timetable_slots_teacher_no_overlap` vs `sch_timetable_slots_room_no_overlap`) is decoded into a friendly `409 Conflict` with the conflicting actor's name (e.g. "Teacher James Rivera is already scheduled for Period 1 during the requested date range" or "Room Room 101 is already scheduled for Period 1 during the requested date range" — name lookups via separate `sch_rooms` / `sch_periods` / `hr_employees` reads on the failure path); 23503 (FK violation) becomes 400; 23505 on `sch_timetable_slots_class_period_from_uq` becomes a different 409. Slot writes emit `sch.timetable.updated` via `KafkaProducerService.emit({sourceModule:'scheduling'})`. `RoomService` (4 endpoints: `GET /rooms` with optional `availabilityDate` + `availabilityPeriodId` annotation that returns `available: boolean | null` per row by intersecting against active timetable slots that match the period for the supplied date, `GET /rooms/:id`, `POST /rooms` admin, `PATCH /rooms/:id` admin). `RoomBookingService` (4 endpoints: `GET /room-bookings` with `roomId` / `status` / `fromDate` / `toDate` filters, `GET /room-bookings/:id`, `POST /room-bookings` write — `assertNoConflicts` checks both existing CONFIRMED bookings whose time range overlaps **and** active timetable slots whose period clock-time on the booking's ISO weekday overlaps the booking window (the schema does NOT enforce booking-vs-slot conflict — it's an app-layer gate; per Step 2's out-of-scope decision), `PATCH /room-bookings/:id/cancel` write — owner or admin only). `RoomChangeRequestService` (5 endpoints: `GET /room-change-requests` write — non-admins see only their own rows via row-scope filter on `requested_by = actor.employeeId`, admins see all; `GET /room-change-requests/:id`, `POST /room-change-requests` write — refuses if the slot's `teacher_id` is set and not the actor (admins bypass), reads `current_room_id` from the slot rather than trusting the client; `PATCH /room-change-requests/:id/approve` admin (requires `approvedRoomId` if the original request had `requestedRoomId=null`); `PATCH /room-change-requests/:id/reject` admin). All 5 services use `tenant.schoolId` from `getCurrentTenant()` for the school-scoped fields rather than reading from `school_config` (more direct, since the tenant context is always populated). The `actor.employeeId` populated by `ActorContextService.resolveActor(...)` is the row-scope key for change requests + bookings + room change request submitters; admins bypass the row check. `SchedulingModule` imports `TenantModule` + `IamModule` + `KafkaModule` and lives at index 5 in `AppModule.imports` between `HrModule` and `NotificationsModule`. admin `POST /timetable/slots` for Period 7 (free LESSON) + Library + null teacher succeeds 201; teacher `POST /room-bookings` for Library 2030-09-15 09:00–10:00 returns 201; second booking for the same window returns `409 — "Room is already booked for an overlapping window (booking …)"`; only PENDING requests can be approved"); `set-default` round trip flips Early Dismissal → default, then back to Standard Day → default cleanly via the partial-UNIQUE-aware atomic helper; `GET /rooms?availabilityDate=2026-05-15&availabilityPeriodId={P1}` returns 10 rooms with Room 101 marked `available=false` (Rivera's Algebra slot covers it) and the other 9 marked `available=true`. **All smoke residue cleaned up** (`DELETE FROM sch_room_change_requests` + `sch_room_bookings` for the smoke rows) so `tenant_demo` is back to seed state for downstream Steps 6–10.

**Step 6 lands the calendar / coverage NestJS side at `apps/api/src/scheduling/`** — 4 services + 3 controllers + 16 endpoints + 1 Kafka consumer (`CoverageConsumer`) + 2 Kafka emits (`sch.coverage.needed`, `sch.coverage.assigned`). `CalendarService` (5 endpoints under `sch-003:read` / `sch-003:write` admin gates: `GET /calendar` with `fromDate` / `toDate` / `eventType` / `includeDrafts` filters — non-admins only ever see published; admins with `includeDrafts=true` see drafts too. `GET /calendar/:id` (drafts hidden from non-admins by 404). `POST /calendar` admin — schedule-aware time-shape assertion (`allDay=true` clears times; `allDay=false` requires `startTime < endTime`). `PATCH /calendar/:id` admin — when `allDay` toggles to `true` the UPDATE clears `start_time` + `end_time` in the same statement so the schema's time-consistency CHECK never fires mid-flight. `DELETE /calendar/:id` admin. `GET /calendar/day/:date` — the resolution endpoint that the calendar UI hits for a single day; reads override → published events with `bell_schedule_id` → school's `is_default=true` schedule → none, returns `{date, resolvedFrom: 'OVERRIDE'|'EVENT'|'DEFAULT'|'NONE', isSchoolDay, bellScheduleId, bellScheduleName, overrideId, overrideReason, eventIds[]}`). `DayOverrideService` (3 endpoints: `GET /calendar/overrides`, `POST /calendar/overrides` `sch-003:admin`, `DELETE /calendar/overrides/:date` `sch-003:admin`; UNIQUE(school_id, override_date) handled at the service layer with a 409 instead of letting the schema raise — better UX). `CoverageService` (4 endpoints under `sch-004:read` / `sch-004:write`: `GET /coverage` daily board with `fromDate` / `toDate` / `status` filters — non-admin staff see only rows where they are the absent or assigned employee; `GET /coverage/:id`; `PATCH /coverage/:id/assign` admin — locks the row with `FOR UPDATE`, flips OPEN→ASSIGNED, populates `assigned_substitute_id` + `assigned_at`, INSERTs the matching `sch_substitution_timetable` row in the same transaction, then emits `sch.coverage.assigned` with the full join shape outside the tx so the substitute receives an IN_APP notification through the Cycle 3 pipeline; `PATCH /coverage/:id/cancel` admin — drops any matching substitution row in the same tx so the substitute's day-view stops showing the cover, then flips status=CANCELLED). `SubstitutionService` (2 read-only endpoints: `GET /substitutions?fromDate=&toDate=` and `GET /substitutions/teacher/:employeeId?fromDate=&toDate=`; substitution rows are written exclusively by `CoverageService.assign` — there's no direct INSERT path). **`CoverageConsumer` (the long-awaited piece — Cycle 4's `hr.leave.coverage_needed` finally has a consumer)**: subscribes to `dev.hr.leave.coverage_needed` under group `coverage-consumer` using the same `unwrapEnvelope` + `processWithIdempotency` pattern as Cycle 3's notification consumers. Per inbound event, enumerates every weekday (Mon–Fri) date in `[startDate, endDate]`, joins through `sch_timetable_slots → sch_periods` for each `affectedClasses[].classId`, filters slots whose date range covers each date AND whose period `day_of_week` is NULL or matches the date's ISO weekday, then INSERTs one `sch_coverage_requests` row per matching `(slot, date)` pair with status=OPEN. `UNIQUE(timetable_slot_id, coverage_date)` is the schema-side belt-and-braces dedup — Kafka redelivery raises 23505 and the consumer swallows it. The deterministic event_id from REVIEW-CYCLE4 MAJOR 3 is the primary dedup gate (`processWithIdempotency` claims after success, so transient DB failures are retried). When new rows land, emits `sch.coverage.needed` with `{leaveRequestId, employeeId, startDate, endDate, createdCoverageIds[]}` so the Step 8 admin UI can react. **Build clean** (`pnpm --filter @campusos/api build`). All 16 new routes mapped on boot. The consumer subscribes successfully on boot (`Subscribed: groupId=coverage-consumer topics=dev.hr.leave.coverage_needed`). **Live verification on `tenant_demo` (10 scenarios):** parent `GET /calendar` returns 4 published events; admin with `includeDrafts=true` sees all 5 (Senior Prom DRAFT included); student passing `includeDrafts=true` still gets only 4 (gate-tier permission gates plus service-tier double-check); `GET /calendar/day/2026-02-07` resolves to `{resolvedFrom: 'OVERRIDE', isSchoolDay: false, overrideReason: 'Winter storm closure'}`; `GET /calendar/day/2026-04-15` (within Spring Break) resolves to `{resolvedFrom: 'DEFAULT', isSchoolDay: true, bellScheduleName: 'Standard Day', eventIds: [<spring break>]}` because the seeded Spring Break event has no `bell_schedule_id` override; `GET /calendar/day/2026-09-15` (regular weekday) resolves to `{resolvedFrom: 'DEFAULT', bellScheduleName: 'Standard Day', events: 0}`; `GET /coverage` returns the seeded ASSIGNED row Park-covers-Rivera-2026-03-09; `GET /substitutions` returns the matching substitution row. Permission denials all return 403 (parent calendar admin POST, student day-override POST, teacher coverage assign). Calendar event create-as-draft → parent doesn't see it → admin patches `isPublished=true` → parent sees it → cleanup delete returns 200. Day override create-resolve-delete round trip clean. **End-to-end CoverageConsumer flow verified live**: Rivera submits a 1-day sick leave for 2026-09-23 (Wednesday) → admin approves → within 1 second the consumer chain (`hr.leave.approved` → `LeaveNotificationConsumer.emitCoverageNeeded` → `hr.leave.coverage_needed` → `CoverageConsumer.handle`) creates 6 OPEN coverage rows (one per Rivera class — Algebra/English/Biology/World History/Geometry/Chemistry — Periods 1–6), one per class for that single date; admin assigns Park to Period 1 Algebra → status=ASSIGNED + `assignedSubstituteName=Linda Park` + `assignedAt` populated → matching `sch_substitution_timetable` row materialises in Room 101; admin cancels the assigned row → status=CANCELLED + the substitution row is dropped (the substitute's day-view stops showing the cover); the other 5 OPEN rows untouched. **All smoke residue cleaned up** (DELETE FROM `sch_coverage_requests` + `hr_leave_requests` for the smoke 2026-09-23 + restored Rivera's Sick balance) so `tenant_demo` is back to seed state.

**Cycle 4 (HR & Workforce Core) is COMPLETE + APPROVED at `76ddf03` (REVIEW-CYCLE4-CHATGPT — final verdict). Round 1 against `efbcb44` returned REJECT pending 1 BLOCKING + 3 MAJOR; Round 2 against `76ddf03` returned APPROVED** after all four fixes (`bda8a16`) plus the CI-fix commit (TS2347 in seed-hr + Prettier drift, `76ddf03`) landed. Cycle 4 ships clean. **REVIEW-CYCLE4 fixes:** (1) BLOCKING — `LeaveService.{approve,reject,cancel}` now `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the request row inside the same transaction that writes the balance + status, so concurrent admin approves serialise on the row lock and the second one re-reads `status='APPROVED'` and 400s. Verified live with 5 parallel approve curls — 1 won, 4 got 400, balance moved cleanly. (2) MAJOR — `ActorContextService.resolveEmployeeId` now resolves `employment_status IN ('ACTIVE','ON_LEAVE')`; TERMINATED + SUSPENDED stay excluded. ON_LEAVE employees keep portal access (own profile, balances, requests) — TERMINATED still 404s on `/employees/me`. (3) MAJOR — `TrainingComplianceService.getDashboard` accepts `actor.isSchoolAdmin` OR a tenant-scope-chain `hr-004:admin` check via `permissionCheckService.hasAnyPermissionInTenant`. The `apps.tsx` tile already gates on the same union, so UI + API agree. (4) MAJOR — `hr.leave.coverage_needed` republishes now use a deterministic event_id derived from `sha1(inbound_event_id + ':hr.leave.coverage_needed.v1')` formatted as a v5-shaped UUID, plus `correlationId = inbound.event_id`. A Kafka redelivery republish carries the exact same event_id, so Cycle 5's future consumer idempotency catches the dup before doing the work twice. Optional `eventId` field added to `EnvelopeOptions` + `EmitOptions` to enable this pattern for future republishers. Verified live — Python independently computed the expected hash and matched the wire envelope; v5 marker correctly set.

Step 0 retired the Cycle 2 DEVIATION 4 mapping; Steps 1–4 added 17 hr\_\* tables (74 tenant tables total); Step 5 seeded 4 employees + 5 positions + 4 certs + 4 compliance rows + 8 onboarding tasks; Steps 6–7 shipped 23 HR endpoints + 5 Kafka emits + the LeaveNotificationConsumer; Steps 8–9 shipped 7 HR web routes + 3 launchpad tiles (Staff / Leave / Compliance) + 16 hooks. **Step 10 lands `docs/cycle4-cat-script.md`** — the reproducible end-to-end vertical slice CAT, verified live against `tenant_demo` on 2026-04-28. The script wraps a 4-scenario bridge-verification block (Step 0 carry-over: 4 hr_employees rows, 0 orphans across the 4 bridged columns, 74 tenant base tables, 0 cross-schema FKs) around the 9 plan scenarios: directory list (4 employees), employee profile + certifications + balances, submit + Kafka envelope verified on the wire, admin approve + balance update from used 2 → 3 / pending 1 → 0, `hr.leave.coverage_needed` republish with all 6 of Rivera's classes inline (Algebra 1 → Chemistry — for Cycle 5 Scheduling to consume), 3 IN_APP notifications enqueued and SENT (2 admins on requested + Rivera on approved), compliance dashboard amber row for Rivera's Teaching Licence at 60 days, 6 permission denial paths covering both gate-tier (parent/student no HR codes) and admin-tier (teacher cannot approve / verify cert / read dashboard) checks. **All 16 checks pass.** No new code in the closeout commit; the seed inconsistency caught during the Step 7 smoke (Rivera PD pending=0 vs PENDING request for 1d) was fixed in Step 7's commit (`70b6cf3`), so the fresh provision running this CAT produces the correct shape from the start. **Cycle 4 ships clean to the post-cycle architecture review.**

**Step 9 closes the HR UI.** Two new launchpad tiles via the single-source `apps.tsx` catalogue: a **Leave** tile under `hr-003:read` (every staff persona) using the existing `AttendanceIcon`, and a **Compliance** tile under `sch-001:admin` OR `hr-004:admin` using the existing `CheckCircleIcon`. Four new pages: `/leave` (employee view — balance cards with `used + pending` two-tone progress bar / `available` headline; request history with status pills; per-row Cancel button on PENDING requests with a `window.confirm` guard, wired to `useCancelLeaveRequest`); `/leave/new` (request form — leave-type dropdown defaulted to the first active type, `?startDate`/`?endDate` `<input type="date">`, `daysRequested` auto-calc from the date range with half-day support and a manual override, optional reason, live balance hint for the selected type, amber warning when daysRequested exceeds available, submit via `useSubmitLeaveRequest` then `router.push('/leave')` + toast); `/leave/approvals` (admin queue gated on `sch-001:admin` — non-admins see an empty-state explaining admin-only; lists every PENDING via `useLeaveRequests({status:'PENDING'})`; per-row Approve / Reject buttons open a Modal with optional review-notes textarea; Approve modal uses primary CTA, Reject uses red CTA; Modal mutations via `useApproveLeaveRequest(req.id)` / `useRejectLeaveRequest(req.id)` then close + toast); `/compliance` (admin dashboard — 3-stat header card row Active employees / With gaps / Compliant %, three filter chips (All / Has gaps / Fully compliant), per-employee row with `compliantCount / amberCount / redCount` summary pills + a `View profile` link to `/staff/:id` + a Details toggle that expands the per-requirement rows with green/amber/red urgency pills inline). Build clean: `/leave` 5.66 kB, `/leave/new` 5.74 kB, `/leave/approvals` 6.06 kB, `/compliance` 5.65 kB First Load JS.

**Step 8 lands the first HR web surface.** A new "Staff" tile appears on the home launchpad and in the sidebar for any user with `hr-001:read` (driven by the single-source `apps/web/src/components/shell/apps.tsx::getAppsForUser`, using the existing `PeopleIcon`). Three pages: `/staff` (searchable directory list — avatar + full name + primary position title + employee number + email; admin-only `Include inactive` checkbox; client-side search wired to the API's `?search=` and `?includeInactive=` query string); `/staff/[id]` (tabbed profile — Info / Certifications / Leave / Documents; Info tab is always visible to anyone with `hr-001:read`; the other three tabs render only for the owning employee or for school admins, gated by comparing `useMyEmployee().data.id` to the route id and checking `sch-001:admin`); and `/staff/me` (client-side redirect that calls `useMyEmployee` then `router.replace('/staff/:id')`, with a clean "no employee record" empty state for non-staff personas). Certifications tab shows a 4-stat summary (Requirements / Compliant / Expiring / Non-compliant) plus a per-cert list with green/amber/red urgency pills derived from `daysUntilExpiry` + `verificationStatus`, and a per-requirement breakdown joined to the seeded compliance rows. Leave tab shows balances (own profile only — admin viewing someone else gets a hint message) and the request history (admin sees all rows for the target employee). Documents tab is a list view; uploads land in Step 9. **`apps/web/src/lib/types.ts` extended** with the full HR DTO surface (EmployeeDto, EmployeePositionDto, PositionDto, EmployeeDocumentDto, CertificationDto, LeaveTypeDto, LeaveBalanceDto, LeaveRequestDto, ComplianceRowDto, EmployeeComplianceDto, ComplianceDashboardDto + payload types). **`apps/web/src/hooks/use-hr.ts` (new)** exposes 16 hooks: `useEmployees` (refetch on focus), `useEmployee`, `useMyEmployee`, `usePositions` (5 min stale), `useEmployeeDocuments`, `useEmployeeCertifications`, `useExpiringCertifications` (60 s poll), `useEmployeeCompliance`, `useComplianceDashboard` (60 s poll), `useLeaveTypes` (5 min stale), `useMyLeaveBalances`, `useLeaveRequests`, plus 5 mutations (`useSubmitLeaveRequest`, `useApproveLeaveRequest`, `useRejectLeaveRequest`, `useCancelLeaveRequest`, `useVerifyCertification`) — every mutation invalidates the affected query keys. Each hook accepts an `enabled` boolean so persona gating doesn't fire 403 calls. Build clean: `pnpm --filter @campusos/web build` ships `/staff` 6.18 kB, `/staff/[id]` 6.49 kB, `/staff/me` 2.34 kB First Load JS.

**Step 7 lands the leave / cert / compliance API surface plus the first HR Kafka consumer.** `LeaveService` exposes 7 endpoints (`GET /leave-types`, `GET /leave/me/balances`, `GET /leave-requests`, `GET /leave-requests/:id`, `POST /leave-requests`, `PATCH /leave-requests/:id/{approve,reject,cancel}`) and emits 4 Kafka events on every transition (`hr.leave.requested`, `hr.leave.approved`, `hr.leave.rejected`, `hr.leave.cancelled`) with `sourceModule:'hr'`. Submit / approve / reject / cancel each run in `executeInTenantTransaction` — balance UPDATEs respect the non-negative CHECKs from migration 012, so a cancel that would underflow `pending` or `used` fails loudly with a 23514 instead of silently corrupting totals. Per-employee balance reads return one row per leave type (zeros for types with no balance row yet) and surface a derived `available = accrued - used - pending`. `CertificationService` exposes 4 endpoints (`GET /employees/:id/certifications`, `POST /employees/:id/certifications`, `GET /certifications/:id`, `PATCH /certifications/:id/verify`, plus admin `GET /certifications/expiring-soon`) with the same own-or-admin row-scope guard as documents and a `daysUntilExpiry` field computed from today; `verify` is admin-only and emits `hr.certification.verified`. `TrainingComplianceService` exposes 2 endpoints (`GET /employees/:id/compliance` and admin `GET /compliance/dashboard`) with a derived `urgency` tier (green / amber / red) computed from `is_compliant` + `days_until_due`. The dashboard always includes every ACTIVE employee even when they have zero compliance rows (LEFT-side roster). `LeaveNotificationConsumer` (consumer group `leave-notification-consumer`) subscribes to all 4 leave topics, notifies admins on `requested`, notifies the submitter on `approved` / `rejected`, and on `approved` republishes `hr.leave.coverage_needed` with the affected class ids resolved via `sis_class_teachers` for the Cycle 5 Scheduling consumer. **HR endpoint count is now 23** (12 from Step 6 + 11 from Step 7). Build clean, all routes mapped on boot, leave-notification-consumer subscribes successfully (after pre-creating the 6 dev `dev.hr.*` topics — the same auto-creation race that affects Cycle 3's audience-fan-out worker on a fresh broker). **Live verification on `tenant_demo` (22 scenarios):** 5 leave types listed; teacher's seeded balances show non-zero used/pending; admin queue surfaces the 1 PENDING PD request; teacher submits a 1.5-day Sick request → `pending` jumps to 1.5; admin approves → `pending` drops to 0 and `used` rises 2 → 3.5; `hr.leave.requested` notifies the 2 admin accounts (Mitchell + Platform Admin) and `hr.leave.approved` notifies Rivera, all 3 rows SENT to Redis ZADD inbox; **`hr.leave.coverage_needed` published to `dev.hr.leave.coverage_needed` with all 6 of Rivera's classes inline** (Algebra 1 / English 9 / Biology / World History / Geometry / Chemistry); teacher cancels the seeded PD request → `pending` correctly returns to 0; admin POST cert + admin PATCH verify works end-to-end; teacher denied cert verify with 403 (`hr-004:write` admin-only); parent denied with 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS at the gate; `/certifications/expiring-soon` returns Rivera's Teaching Licence with the dynamic 60-day expiry from Step 5's seed. **Bug caught and fixed by the smoke:** Step 5 seed had Rivera's PD balance row at `pending=0` while also seeding a PENDING PD request for 1 day — the schema's `pending_chk >= 0` correctly rejected the cancel underflow, exposing the seed inconsistency. `seed-hr.ts` updated to set Rivera PD `pending=1.0` to match the seeded request; the live demo tenant patched in-place so the smoke could complete. Personal Leave's stale `used=1, pending=1` (no matching seeded request) reset to zeros for the same reason.

**Step 6 lands the first HR API surface at `apps/api/src/hr/`** with three services and 12 endpoints. `EmployeeService` handles the staff directory list (`GET /employees`, joined to `iam_person` for first/last name + `platform_users` for email + the most recent `hr_employee_positions` row for the primary position title), single-record reads (`GET /employees/:id` and `GET /employees/me` which resolves the calling user via `actor.employeeId` and 404s if the actor is parent/student/Platform Admin), admin-only create (validates the supplied `personId` + `accountId` against the platform schema, links them to a freshly minted `hr_employees` row inside one `executeInTenantTransaction`, optionally seeds a primary `hr_employee_positions` assignment from `initialPositionId`), and admin-only patch (employee_number / employment_type / employment_status / termination_date — dynamic SET-clause builder so callers can update one field or many). `PositionService` is admin-only for writes (`POST` / `PATCH` gated on `hr-001:admin`), reads on `hr-001:read`; the list query returns each position with `activeAssignments` (count of `hr_employee_positions` rows where `effective_to IS NULL`) and the joined `sis_departments.name` for the soft `department_id` ref. `EmployeeDocumentService` enforces a row-scope guard (`assertCanAccess` — admin OR `actor.employeeId === employeeId`, otherwise 403); list returns non-archived rows joined to `hr_document_types` for the type label; create validates the document type is active + the employee exists; archive flips `is_archived=true` (soft delete) — hard delete is intentionally not exposed. The document column `uploaded_by` is set from `actor.accountId` so the audit trail records the platform user, not the employee record. **DTOs use `class-validator`** with `IsIn` arrays for the employment_type and employment_status enums (keeps the values in sync with the SQL CHECK constraints). The position list controller uses `class-transformer` `@Transform` to coerce `?includeInactive=true` from the query string into a boolean. `HrModule` imports `TenantModule` + `IamModule` and lives at index 4 in `AppModule.imports` between `ClassroomModule` and `NotificationsModule`. Build clean, all 12 routes mapped on boot. Live verification on `tenant_demo`: principal@ sees 4 employees in `/employees` (Mitchell/Rivera/Park/Hayes ordered by last name, each with employee_number + primary position title); teacher@ `/employees/me` resolves Rivera with `positions=1` and `primaryPositionTitle='Teacher'`; principal@ `/positions` returns 5 (incl. the unassigned Administrative Assistant with `activeAssignments=0`); parent@ blocked at the permission gate on `/employees` and `/employees/me` with `hr-001:read` required; student@ blocked similarly on `/positions`; counsellor@ trying to read Rivera's documents gets a clean 403 from the row-scope check (own documents OR admin only); teacher@ POST `/positions` returns 403 (`hr-001:admin` required); principal@ creates a "Smoke Position" then PATCHes `isActive=false` round-trip; principal@ POST `/employees` with bogus UUIDs returns 400 from the validators (proves admin path is reachable to admins).

**Step 5 layers data on top of the schema:** `seed-hr.ts` extended with idempotent layers (each gates on its own row count) — 5 positions (Teacher, Principal, VP, Counsellor, Administrative Assistant) + 4 position assignments mapping the 4 employees to their roles, 5 leave types (Sick / Personal / Bereavement / PD / Unpaid) + 20 per-(employee × type) balances for the current academic year (Rivera has used some sick + personal so the CAT shows non-zero used/pending), 2 sample leave requests for Rivera (1 APPROVED sick leave from March, 1 PENDING PD day for next month), 4 certifications (Rivera Texas Teaching Licence VERIFIED + First Aid + Safeguarding L1; Mitchell DBS Enhanced VERIFIED — **Rivera's licence is seeded with `expiry_date = today + 60 days` so it dynamically drives the CAT compliance dashboard amber row**), 4 training requirements (3 school-wide ANNUAL/BIENNIAL + 1 position-specific Teaching Licence Renewal), 4 pre-computed compliance rows (Rivera 2 compliant + 1 not-compliant linked to the expiring licence; Mitchell 1 not-compliant Safeguarding), 4 document types (Contract / Background Check / W-4 / Teaching Licence Copy with retention_days populated), and 1 "New Teacher Onboarding" template + 1 NOT_STARTED checklist for Rivera + 8 tasks (DOCUMENT × 4, TRAINING × 2, SYSTEM_ACCESS × 1, ORIENTATION × 1) covering onboarding from contract through classroom orientation. **`seed-iam.ts` updated:** Teacher role gains HR-001:read + HR-003:read+write + HR-004:read (4 perms, 27 → 31). Staff role same 4 grants (6 → 10). The role-assignment block was rewritten from "if any assignments exist, skip" to "per-user lookup-or-create" so the new `vp@` (Linda Park) and `counsellor@` (Marcus Hayes) staff accounts now get the Staff role + scope assignment without dropping existing assignments. After `tsx src/build-cache.ts`: cache holds 7 account-scope pairs (was 5) — admin/principal 444, teacher 31, student 15, parent 11, vp/counsellor 10. Tenant base table count unchanged at 74 (data only — no DDL).

**Step 4 lands `014_hr_onboarding.sql`** with 3 base tables: `hr_onboarding_templates` (school-scoped catalogue, optional `position_id` for position-specific templates, UNIQUE(school_id, name)), `hr_onboarding_checklists` (per-(employee, template) instance with status NOT_STARTED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED enforced by a multi-column CHECK that started_at and completed_at stay in sync with status, UNIQUE(employee_id, template_id) so a hire can hold at most one checklist per template), `hr_onboarding_tasks` (5 category values DOCUMENT/TRAINING/SYSTEM_ACCESS/ORIENTATION/OTHER, 4 status values PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/SKIPPED, `due_days_from_start INT >= 0` CHECK, multi-column CHECK that `completed_at` is set if and only if status is COMPLETED or SKIPPED). 3 intra-tenant FKs (1 to `hr_employees ON DELETE CASCADE`, 1 to `hr_onboarding_templates`, 1 to `hr_onboarding_checklists ON DELETE CASCADE`). Tenant logical base table count: 74 (was 71). Live verification on `tenant_demo`: all 8 CHECK violations rejected (status enums, status/started-at sync, category enum, due_days negative, completed-at sync), happy-path "New Teacher Onboarding" template with 3 tasks instantiated for Rivera + one task moved to COMPLETED + checklist moved to IN_PROGRESS, UNIQUE(employee_id, template_id) rejects duplicate, ON DELETE CASCADE drops all 3 tasks when the parent checklist is deleted.

**Step 3 lands `013_hr_certifications_and_training.sql`** with 5 base tables: `hr_staff_certifications` (10 certification types — TEACHING_LICENCE, FIRST_AID, SAFEGUARDING_LEVEL1/2, DBS_BASIC/ENHANCED, FOOD_HYGIENE, FIRE_SAFETY_WARDEN, SPECIALIST_SUBJECT, CUSTOM; 4 verification statuses — PENDING/VERIFIED/EXPIRED/REVOKED; ADR-015 followed — `reference_number` + `verification_status` only, never raw DBS payload), `hr_training_requirements` (school-scoped with optional `position_id` for position-specific mandates, frequency CHECK ONE_TIME/ANNUAL/BIENNIAL/TRIENNIAL/CUSTOM with a multi-column CHECK that `custom_frequency_months` is set if and only if frequency=CUSTOM), `hr_training_compliance` (UNIQUE(employee_id, requirement_id) materialised state with `linked_certification_id` FK to `hr_staff_certifications ON DELETE SET NULL` so a deleted cert leaves the compliance row defensible), `hr_cpd_requirements` (UNIQUE(school_id, position_id, academic_year_id) PD/credit-hour mandates), `hr_work_authorisation` (UNIQUE(employee_id) right-to-work with 6 document types, separate `expiry_date` and `reverification_due_date` because some EADs require re-verification on a different cadence). 7 intra-tenant FKs (4 to `hr_employees ON DELETE CASCADE`, 1 to `hr_training_requirements ON DELETE CASCADE`, 1 to `hr_staff_certifications ON DELETE SET NULL`, 1 each to `hr_positions` and `sis_academic_years` non-cascade). Tenant logical base table count: 71 (was 66). Live verification on `tenant_demo`: 7 CHECKs fire (cert type/status/dates, requirement frequency/custom, work-auth type, CPD pd_hours), happy path inserts succeed (Rivera Teaching Licence VERIFIED, ANNUAL renewal requirement, compliance row linked to the cert), ON DELETE SET NULL nulls `linked_certification_id` when the cert is deleted while keeping the compliance row, UNIQUE on `(employee_id, requirement_id)` and on `hr_work_authorisation.employee_id` rejects duplicates, ON DELETE CASCADE on `hr_employees` drops cert + compliance + work_auth rows for a temp employee.

**Step 2 lands `012_hr_leave_management.sql`** with 3 base tables: `hr_leave_types` (per-school catalogue with `is_paid` / `accrual_rate` / optional `max_balance`), `hr_leave_balances` (UNIQUE(employee_id, leave_type_id, academic_year_id) with `accrued`/`used`/`pending NUMERIC(5,2)` non-negative CHECKs, FK to `sis_academic_years`), and `hr_leave_requests` (status CHECK PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED, half-day `days_requested NUMERIC(4,1) > 0` CHECK, dates CHECK `end_date >= start_date`, an `is_hr_initiated` boolean with a multi-column CHECK that enforces `(is_hr_initiated, hr_initiated_by, hr_initiated_reason)` are all-set or all-null together for HR-initiated leaves like mandatory PD days). 5 intra-tenant FKs (2 to `hr_employees ON DELETE CASCADE`, 2 to `hr_leave_types`, 1 to `sis_academic_years` non-cascade). Tenant logical base table count: 66 (was 63). Approval flow is documented at the schema layer; the Step 7 LeaveService will own the state transitions and Kafka emits (`hr.leave.requested`, `hr.leave.approved`, `hr.leave.rejected`, `hr.leave.cancelled`). Live verification on `tenant_demo`: all 6 CHECKs fire (status, dates, days, hr-initiated mismatch, accrual_rate negative, balance accrued negative), UNIQUE on `(employee, type, year)` rejects duplicates, happy-path multi-insert across all 3 tables succeeds, ON DELETE CASCADE drops 1 balance + 1 request when a temp `hr_employees` row is deleted.

**Step 1 lands 5 base tables on top of `hr_employees`** in the same `011_hr_employees_and_positions.sql` migration: `hr_positions` (UNIQUE(school_id, title), soft FK `department_id` → `sis_departments`, `is_teaching_role` flag), `hr_employee_positions` (DB-enforced FKs to `hr_employees ON DELETE CASCADE` and `hr_positions`, `effective_from`/`effective_to` date range, partial UNIQUE index on `(employee_id) WHERE is_primary AND effective_to IS NULL` so an employee has at most one current primary position, FTE CHECK 0 < fte ≤ 1.000), `hr_emergency_contacts` (CASCADE on employee delete, partial UNIQUE on `is_primary`), `hr_document_types` (UNIQUE(school_id, name), retention_days CHECK > 0), `hr_employee_documents` (CASCADE on employee delete, FK to document_type, signed-URL pattern documented in COMMENT). 5 new intra-tenant FKs, 0 cross-schema FKs. Tenant logical base table count: 63 (was 58). Live verification on `tenant_demo`: every CHECK fires (dates, FTE > 1.0, retention 0, file_size_bytes -1), FK rejection returns clean ERROR, happy-path multi-insert across all 5 tables succeeds, ON DELETE CASCADE on a temporary `hr_employees` row drops all 3 child rows. **Splitter trap struck again** — even block-comment text containing `;` cuts the migration mid-comment because the splitter splits on every semicolon regardless of quoting context (block-comment, string literal, anywhere). The 011 migration's header now spells out "no semicolons" instead of using a literal `;` as an example.

`packages/database/prisma/tenant/migrations/011_hr_employees_and_positions.sql` lands the `hr_employees` table (soft FK to `platform.iam_person` via UNIQUE `person_id` + soft FK to `platform.platform_users` via UNIQUE `account_id`, CHECK constraints on `employment_type` + `employment_status`). `packages/database/src/seed-hr.ts` (idempotent, gated on `hr_employees` row count) inserts 4 employee rows for `tenant_demo` (Mitchell as `principal@`, Rivera as `teacher@`, Park as `vp@`, Hayes as `counsellor@`; the `admin@` Platform Admin persona is intentionally NOT bridged), then runs four `UPDATE … FROM hr_employees WHERE e.person_id = t.column` bridge statements inside one `executeInTenantTransaction` to re-point `sis_class_teachers.teacher_employee_id`, `cls_grades.teacher_id`, `cls_lessons.teacher_id`, and `cls_student_progress_notes.author_id` from `iam_person.id` to `hr_employees.id`. Live verification: 4 rows inserted, 6 + 62 + 0 + 1 rows bridged across the four columns, 0 orphans. `ActorContextService.resolveActor(...)` now populates `actor.employeeId: string | null` via a tenant-scoped lookup against `hr_employees.person_id`. All staff-side service code substituted: `attendance.service.ts::assertCanWriteClassAttendance`, `assignment.service.ts::{assertCanWriteClass,canReadClass STAFF,isClassManager}`, `gradebook.service.ts::{assertCanViewStudent STAFF,isClassManager}`, `submission.service.ts::{isManagerOfClass,canSeeSubmission STAFF}`, `grade.service.ts::{batchGrade,upsertGrade}` (4 INSERT/UPDATE sites; `ForbiddenException` guard at entry of both write paths since `cls_grades.teacher_id` is NOT NULL), `progress-note.service.ts::{upsert,listForStudent STAFF,assertCanViewStudent STAFF}` (2 INSERT/UPDATE sites + `ForbiddenException` guard), `student.service.ts::visibilityClause STAFF`, `class.service.ts::listForTeacherEmployee` (renamed from `listForTeacherPerson`), `class.service.ts::loadTeachersForClasses` (now joins through `hr_employees` to `iam_person`), `class.controller.ts::my` (resolves actor + passes `actor.employeeId`), `audience-fan-out.worker.ts::audienceClass` (joins through `hr_employees.account_id` to `platform_users` for the CLASS-audience teacher branch). `IamModule` now imports `TenantModule` so `ActorContextService` can do the tenant-scoped lookup. Live smoke against `tenant_demo` confirmed `GET /classes/my` for `teacher@` returns the same 6 classes as before the bridge, `GET /students` returns 15 students via the new STAFF predicate, `GET /classes/:id/gradebook` returns 3 students for the P1 class. The four `COMMENT ON COLUMN` annotations on the bridged columns were rewritten to retire the "TEMPORARY HR-EMPLOYEE IDENTITY MAPPING" wording and adopt the permanent "Soft FK to hr_employees(id) per ADR-055" convention. **Migration gotcha re-confirmed:** the SQL splitter in `provision-tenant.ts` cuts on `;` even inside string literals — the `COMMENT ON COLUMN` strings cannot contain `;`. Use commas / "and" / em-dashes instead. Tripped this on the first re-provision attempt; the four updated COMMENTs and the new `hr_employees.school_id` COMMENT all use punctuation that survives the splitter. (Steps 1–10 of Cycle 4 — schemas for positions, leave, certifications, training compliance, onboarding, and the corresponding NestJS modules + UI + CAT — remain to ship; see `docs/campusos-cycle4-implementation-plan.html` and `HANDOFF-CYCLE4.md` for the plan.)

Cycle 0 (Platform Foundation) is COMPLETE. **Cycle 1 (SIS Core + Attendance) is COMPLETE — all 11 steps done. Post-cycle architecture review fixes (REVIEW-CYCLE1) landed.** Schema, seed, SIS API, Attendance API + Kafka emits, web UI shell, Teacher Dashboard, Attendance Taking UI with confirm modal + batch submit, Parent Dashboard + child attendance calendar + absence-request form, AdminDashboard (school-wide overview + pending-absence queue), and a verified end-to-end vertical slice (`docs/cycle1-cat-script.md`). The post-cycle review tightened tenant isolation (`SET LOCAL search_path` inside an interactive tx), added row-level authorization to student reads, gated attendance writes by `sis_class_teachers` membership, and replaced cross-scope admin checks with a tenant-scope-chain check.

**Cycle 3 (Communications) is COMPLETE — all 11 steps done. Post-cycle architecture review APPROVED at commit `592d366` (REVIEW-CYCLE3-CHATGPT — final verdict).** Round 1 at SHA `7c7e3d4` returned REJECT pending two reliability/security fixes; Round 2 at SHA `592d366` returned APPROVED to proceed. The three findings (BLOCKING 1 Kafka consumer error swallowing, BLOCKING 2 NotificationDeliveryWorker SENT-as-in-flight, MAJOR overly-broad `isManager()` scope) were all fixed in `592d366`.

**Reviewer's carry-over for the next cycle:** verify `platform.platform_dlq_messages` is in migrations + available in every environment since the consumer now depends on it. **Already satisfied at the schema level** — the table ships in the platform Prisma migration `20260427211003_add_communications_platform_tables` (Cycle 3 Step 3), and the CI workflow runs `npx prisma migrate deploy --schema=prisma/platform/schema.prisma` so the table is created in CI + every environment that follows the deploy pipeline. The remaining work is operational: wire a DLQ-row dashboard / alert into Phase 2 so a parked poison message gets human attention, not just a quiet row in a table. **REVIEW-CYCLE3 fixes (2026-04-28):** (1) `apps/api/src/kafka/kafka-consumer.service.ts` no longer swallows handler failures — it rethrows so KafkaJS retains the offset, with an in-memory `(group, topic, partition, offset) → attempts` map bounded by `MAX_HANDLER_ATTEMPTS=5` so a poison message gets parked into `platform.platform_dlq_messages` (with `event_id`, `tenant_id`, headers, payload, error_class/message, retry_count) and committed instead of looping forever. Malformed JSON is parked directly without retry since it can't recover. (2) `apps/api/src/notifications/notification-delivery.worker.ts` now uses a proper `PROCESSING` in-flight state — Phase 0 stale-row sweep recovers PROCESSING > 5 minutes back to PENDING (preserving attempts so MAX_ATTEMPTS still bounds total retries), Phase 1 SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + UPDATE PROCESSING + processing_started_at, Phase 2 deliver outside the claim tx then UPDATE SENT (only after Redis ZADD + `msg_notification_log` write succeed). New tenant migration `010_msg_queue_processing_state.sql` extends the queue status CHECK to include PROCESSING and adds a `processing_started_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column + partial index. The migration uses `/* */` block-comment style — line `--` headers cause the SQL splitter to filter the entire first statement. Tenant base table count: still 57 (only constraint + column added). (3) `apps/api/src/announcements/announcement.service.ts::isManager()` no longer returns true for any actor with `personType === 'STAFF'` — it now calls `permissionCheckService.hasAnyPermissionInTenant(accountId, schoolId, ['com-002:write'])` so manager status follows the actual permission grant. The IAM seed gives Staff just `com-002:read`, so a staff member is correctly treated as a reader (audience-row-required, no draft visibility) instead of a manager. School admins still bypass via `actor.isSchoolAdmin`. All 4 call sites in the service await the new async helper. CAT smoke (all 7 scenarios) re-verified live against `tenant_demo` after the fixes; queue inspection post-run shows zero rows stuck in PROCESSING (80/80 SENT). Step 1 lands `packages/database/prisma/tenant/migrations/007_msg_messaging.sql` — 6 base messaging tables (`msg_thread_types`, `msg_threads`, `msg_thread_participants`, `msg_messages`, `msg_message_attachments`, `msg_message_reads`) plus 64 HASH partitions of `msg_threads` (per ADR-047, partition key `school_id`) and 24 monthly RANGE partitions of `msg_messages` covering 2025-08 → 2027-08. Soft UUID refs to `platform.platform_users` per ADR-001/020. Composite PKs `(id, school_id)` for `msg_threads` and `(id, created_at)` for `msg_messages` (the partition columns must appear in the unique constraint). FKs from child tables to the partitioned parents follow the `sis_attendance_evidence` precedent — denormalise the partition key onto the child + add an index, no DB-enforced FK. **Step 2 lands `packages/database/prisma/tenant/migrations/008_msg_notifications_and_announcements.sql` — 7 base tables (`msg_alert_types`, `msg_notification_queue`, `msg_notification_preferences`, `msg_notification_log`, `msg_announcements`, `msg_announcement_audiences`, `msg_announcement_reads`) plus 24 monthly RANGE partitions of `msg_notification_log` (sent_at, 2025-08 → 2027-08, matching the messages window). `msg_notification_log` uses composite PK `(id, sent_at)` so the partition column is in the unique constraint. The notification queue does NOT carry a UNIQUE constraint on `idempotency_key` — the partial index on it is for read-side dedup investigation only; authoritative idempotency is Redis SET NX (per the plan, to avoid deadlocks during emergency fan-out). 3 intra-tenant DB-enforced FKs (`msg_announcements.alert_type_id → msg_alert_types`, `msg_announcement_audiences.announcement_id → msg_announcements ON DELETE CASCADE`, `msg_announcement_reads.announcement_id → msg_announcements ON DELETE CASCADE`); all other cross-table refs (queue→user, log→queue, audiences→user) are soft per ADR-001/020. `msg_announcements.audience_ref TEXT` is a polymorphic target field interpreted by the AudienceFanOutWorker (Step 7) based on `audience_type` (CLASS = sis_classes.id as text, YEAR_GROUP = grade label, ROLE = iam role name, ALL_SCHOOL = NULL).** **Step 3 lands `packages/database/prisma/tenant/migrations/009_msg_moderation.sql` (6 base tenant tables — `msg_moderation_policies`, `msg_moderation_log`, `msg_tags`, `msg_user_tags`, `msg_user_blocks`, `msg_admin_access_log` — plus 24 monthly RANGE partitions of `msg_moderation_log` matching the 2025-08 → 2027-08 window) AND a Prisma migration `20260427211003_add_communications_platform_tables` that adds the first platform-schema tables since Cycle 0: `platform_push_tokens` (per-(user, device) push registration with `PushPlatform` enum IOS/ANDROID/WEB) and `platform_dlq_messages` (Kafka dead letter queue with topic/partition/kafka_offset/payload/headers/retry_count/error fields). The moderation policy table is three-tier (PLATFORM/DISTRICT/BUILDING) with each tenant carrying its own copy of the higher-tier policies that apply to it, so the moderation interceptor consults a single tenant table without cross-schema reads. The moderation log holds a soft denormalised `(message_id, message_created_at)` ref to the partitioned `msg_messages` (matches the `msg_message_attachments` precedent from Step 1) plus a DB-enforced `policy_id → msg_moderation_policies(id)` FK that PostgreSQL replicates onto each of the 24 monthly partitions (25 FK rows in `pg_constraint`, expected). `msg_user_tags.tag_id → msg_tags(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` is the second DB-enforced FK; `msg_user_blocks` carries a `blocker_id <> blocked_id` self-block CHECK; `msg_admin_access_log.reason` is NOT NULL because every admin read of a non-participant private thread must be FERPA-justified.** **Step 4 lands `packages/database/src/seed-messaging.ts` (idempotent, gated on `msg_thread_types` row count) — populates the demo tenant with 4 thread types (TEACHER_PARENT, CLASS_DISCUSSION, ADMIN_STAFF, SYSTEM_NOTIFICATION), 3 sample threads + 6 participants + 10 messages + 4 message reads (Rivera↔David Chen Maya progress check-in, P1 Algebra Q&A class discussion, Sarah↔Rivera staff thread), 3 alert types (GENERAL_ANNOUNCEMENT, PARENT_INFORMATIONAL, WEATHER_CLOSURE), 40 notification preferences (5 test users × 8 notification types — `attendance.{tardy,absent}`, `grade.published`, `progress_note.published`, `absence.{requested,reviewed}`, `message.posted`, `announcement.published` — with EMAIL channel enabled for `grade.published` + `attendance.tardy`, and 22:00–07:00 quiet hours on the parent), 2 moderation policies (PLATFORM-scope BLOCK profanity policy + BUILDING-scope FLAG_FOR_REVIEW policy for substance/bullying keywords), 2 announcements (ALL_SCHOOL "Welcome Back" + ROLE=PARENT "Parent-Teacher Conference Dates", both published) with 15 audience rows + 4 read marks, and 3 notification queue rows (1 SENT tardy notification for David, 1 SENT grade.published for Maya, 1 PENDING message-posted for David) plus 2 corresponding notification_log delivery rows. Adds `seed:messaging` to `packages/database/package.json`. The seed targets `tenant_demo` only (matching `seed-sis` / `seed-classroom` precedent — `tenant_test` stays empty for tests). `seed-iam.ts` was extended to add `COM-002:read` to the Student and Staff roles (previously held only by Teacher/Parent/School Admin/Platform Admin) — closes the plan's "Announcements read to all + write to Teacher/Admin" requirement; COM-001 read/write was already on Teacher/Parent/Student, COM-003 already on Platform/School Admin via `everyFunction`. Effective access cache rebuilt: Student now 15 perms (was 14), Staff now 6 (was 5).** **Step 5 lands the notification pipeline at `apps/api/src/notifications/`: 5 Kafka consumers (AttendanceNotificationConsumer for `att.student.marked_tardy` + `att.student.marked_absent`, GradeNotificationConsumer for `cls.grade.published`, ProgressNoteNotificationConsumer for `cls.progress_note.published`, AbsenceRequestNotificationConsumer for `att.absence.requested` + `att.absence.reviewed`, and the forward-compatible MessageNotificationConsumer for `msg.message.posted` whose producer ships in Step 6) + `NotificationQueueService` + `NotificationDeliveryWorker` + `RedisService` (first ioredis usage in the API). Each consumer follows the Cycle 2 GradebookSnapshotWorker pattern: read the ADR-057 envelope (with header fallback), `IdempotencyService.isClaimed` read-only check on arrival, resolve recipients inside `runWithTenantContextAsync`, enqueue via `NotificationQueueService`, then `claim()` after success (REVIEW-CYCLE2 BLOCKING 2 at-least-once). Recipient resolution: attendance/grade/progress-note consumers fan out to portal-enabled guardians via `sis_student_guardians` (`portal_access=true AND receives_reports=true AND g.account_id IS NOT NULL`); grade + progress-note also notify the student themself via the `sis_students → platform_students → platform_users` lookup; absence-request fans out to school admins (resolved via the `sch-001:admin` row in `iam_effective_access_cache` joined to `iam_scope`/`iam_scope_type`, school + platform scopes per ADR-036) on submission and to the original submitter (`sis_absence_requests.submitted_by`) on review; message-posted notifies every active non-sender thread participant + bumps the per-(user, thread) Redis HASH unread counter that Step 6's UnreadCountService reads. `NotificationQueueService.enqueue()` does Redis SET NX on `notif:idem:{subdomain}:{key}` (7-day TTL — authoritative dedup per ADR-001/020 since the DB table has no UNIQUE on `idempotency_key`), reads `msg_notification_preferences` for the (recipient, type) pair (default IN_APP if missing), checks 22:00–07:00-style quiet hours (wraps midnight; defers `scheduled_for` to the next quiet-end boundary), and INSERTs a PENDING row with the supplied JSON payload + `correlation_id`. `NotificationDeliveryWorker` polls every 10s (configurable via `NOTIFICATION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`) — for every active row in `platform.schools` it enters tenant context, runs `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 25` on `msg_notification_queue` for `status='PENDING' AND scheduled_for <= now()`, flips rows to SENT in the same tx (atomic in-flight flag), then per-row delivers IN_APP via Redis ZADD on `notif:inapp:{accountId}` (capped at 100 entries via ZREMRANGEBYRANK) and stubs EMAIL/PUSH/SMS with a `[stub-deliver]` log line. Every delivery (real or stub) writes a `msg_notification_log` row with `status=DELIVERED` for IN_APP and `SENT` for the stubbed channels. Failure path: bumps `attempts`, flips back to PENDING with a 30-second `scheduled_for` backoff for up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 retries before settling on FAILED. Best-effort connection: RedisService and KafkaConsumerService both no-op gracefully when Redis or Kafka are unreachable in dev (matching the existing KafkaProducerService pattern). NotificationsModule wired into AppModule between ClassroomModule and the global guards. **Cycle 2 (Classroom + Assignments + Grading) is COMPLETE — all 10 steps done. Post-cycle architecture review APPROVED at commit `d876e86` (REVIEW-CYCLE2-CHATGPT — final verdict).** The post-cycle review tightened `GET /classes/:classId/gradebook` to manager-only (permission gate switched from `tch-003:read` → `tch-003:write` and row-scope from `assertCanReadClass` → `assertCanWriteClass`, closing a latent grade-data leak to students/parents who held `tch-003:read`); rewrote the GradebookSnapshotWorker idempotency from at-most-once to at-least-once (read-only `IdempotencyService.isClaimed` on arrival, debounce-entry tracks contributing event-ids, `claim()` only fires AFTER a successful recompute, transient DB failures retry on the next event); and documented the temporary HR-employee identity mapping that columns named `*_employee_id` / `cls_grades.teacher_id` / `cls_lessons.teacher_id` / `cls_student_progress_notes.author_id` currently hold `iam_person.id` directly until the HR module ships — annotated in the migration SQL via `COMMENT ON COLUMN`. The ADR-057 event envelope is deferred to Cycle 3 (Communications) where multiple producers and consumers will arrive together; the grade-emit headers (`event-id`, `tenant-id`, `tenant-subdomain`) already carry the three fields the worker reads, so the migration is additive. Migrations `005_cls_lessons_and_assignments.sql` (7 tables) and `006_cls_submissions_and_grading.sql` (8 tables) add the full M21 Classroom schema — 15 tenant tables total. ADR-010 (gradebook snapshots are async-only) is enforced at the schema layout level: `cls_grades` and `cls_gradebook_snapshots` are physically separate tables with no FK or trigger linking them; the Step 5 grade write path was end-to-end-verified to never touch the snapshot table. AI / human boundary: `cls_ai_grading_jobs` and `cls_submission_question_grades.ai_*` columns store AI suggestions; `cls_grades` has zero `ai_*` columns and is written only by teacher action. 28 intra-tenant FKs across the two migrations; zero cross-schema FKs. Step 3 (`seed-classroom.ts`) seeds 1 grading scale, 5 assignment types, 18 per-class categories (Homework 30 / Assessments 50 / Participation 20), 12 assignments, 80 submissions, 62 grades (53 published), 41 gradebook snapshots, and 1 progress note for Maya — and adds TCH-002:read (Parent), TCH-004:read (Student), TCH-004:read+write (Teacher) to the role-permission map. Step 4 lands AssignmentService + CategoryService + their controllers — 7 endpoints under `tch-002:read/write` with the same row-level auth pattern as Cycle 1 (admin → all; teacher → assigned classes via `sis_class_teachers`; student → enrolled classes; parent → linked-child classes). Step 5 lands SubmissionService + GradeService + GradebookService + ProgressNoteService + 4 controllers — 12 new endpoints (3 `tch-002:*` + 9 `tch-003:*`). Submissions are idempotent upserts by `(assignment, student)`; resubmitting flips status back to `SUBMITTED`. Grade writes (single + batch + publish + unpublish + publish-all) emit `cls.grade.published` / `cls.grade.unpublished` via `KafkaProducerService` and never write to `cls_gradebook_snapshots`. Draft grades are filtered out of student / parent payloads (`rowToDto(row, includeDraftGrade)` flag — manager teacher / admin sees them; everyone else does not). Gradebook reads (`/classes/:id/gradebook`, `/students/:id/gradebook`) join roster ↔ snapshot per resolved term (default = current term). Progress notes upsert by `(class, student, term)` with persona-scoped reads (admins all; teachers their classes; students/parents only `is_*_visible=true` AND `published_at IS NOT NULL`). **Step 6 lands the first Kafka consumer in the system — `GradebookSnapshotWorker` (in `apps/api/src/classroom/`) — backed by `KafkaConsumerService` and `IdempotencyService` (in `apps/api/src/kafka/`). The worker subscribes to `cls.grade.published` and `cls.grade.unpublished` under consumer group `gradebook-snapshot-worker`, debounces 30 seconds per `(schoolId, classId, studentId)`, and recomputes `cls_gradebook_snapshots` using the exact weighted-average algorithm from `seed-classroom.ts` (per-category mean, weighted by category, renormalised over participating categories only). Idempotency is via `platform.platform_event_consumer_idempotency` keyed on `(consumer_group, event_id)`; redelivered events fail the `INSERT` (SQLSTATE 23505) and are dropped before they can reset the debounce. Tenant context is reconstructed at flush time from Kafka headers (`event-id`, `tenant-id`, `tenant-subdomain`) using `runWithTenantContextAsync`, so the worker reuses the same `TenantPrismaService` helpers as the request path. The grade emit (`grade.service.ts::tenantHeaders`) injects these three headers from `getCurrentTenant()` plus a fresh UUIDv7 — forward-compatible with the ADR-057 envelope that lands in Cycle 3.** **Step 7 lands the teacher Assignments UI: a `ClassTabs` shell at `/classes/:id/{attendance,assignments}` (Gradebook tab hidden until Step 8), an assignments list page with type filter / draft visibility for managers / soft-delete confirm, shared `AssignmentForm` for create + edit, and `CategoryWeightModal` that mirrors the API's PUT-by-name semantics with a live "weights must sum to 100" check. New `GET /assignment-types` endpoint exposes the school's type catalogue. Pre-existing lint / Suspense issues in the Cycle 1 dashboards + `/login` were fixed so the web app builds clean — these were transitive (only surfaced once Step 7 needed `next build` to succeed).** **Step 8 lands the teacher Grading UI: a spreadsheet-style gradebook grid at `/classes/:id/gradebook` with color-coded cells × inline editor × per-cell publish toggle × per-assignment "Publish all", a submissions queue at `/assignments/:id/submissions` sorted by grading priority (SUBMITTED first), a single-submission detail page at `/submissions/:id` with grade entry + feedback + publish controls, and a per-student `ProgressNoteModal` launched from the gradebook (auto-loads existing note for the (class, term) pair, upserts on save). The Gradebook tab is now visible across all `/classes/:id/*` routes. **Side fix: `grade.service.ts` now emits `cls.grade.published` on updates to already-published grades** (Step 5 emit gap — only draft↔published transitions were emitting before, so a re-grade of a published row left the snapshot stale). Both `upsertGrade` (single) and `batchGrade` paths now flag rows for emit if they end up published, regardless of prior state. The snapshot worker is idempotent so the redundant emit is harmless.** **Step 9 lands the student & parent grade views: a new student `StudentDashboard` (upcoming-assignment list + per-class average cards), a student `/assignments` inbox across all enrolled classes (filter by class / overdue / next-14-days), `/assignments/:id` student detail + submit form (idempotent resubmit, published-grade reveal), `/grades` per-class average list, `/grades/:classId` per-assignment breakdown, and the parent equivalents — a Grades section on each child card on `ParentDashboard`, `/children/:id/grades` per-child average list, and `/children/:id/grades/:classId` per-class breakdown (incl. parent-visible progress notes). Two new backend endpoints back this: `GET /students/me` (bootstrap the calling student's `studentId` without scanning the list) and `GET /students/:studentId/classes/:classId/grades` (per-(student, class) breakdown — assignments + own submission + own grade, only published rows for non-managers). Sidebar surfaces `Assignments` and `Grades` for STUDENT persona.** **Step 10 lands the Cycle 2 CAT at `docs/cycle2-cat-script.md` — a 9-step reproducible end-to-end walkthrough verified live against `tenant_demo`: teacher creates an assignment → student bootstraps via `/students/me` and submits → teacher grades draft → draft is hidden from the student → teacher publish-all emits `cls.grade.published` → 30-second debounce + idempotent recompute updates `cls_gradebook_snapshots` (worker log captured) → student sees grade via the new per-class endpoint → parent sees the same data through `sis_student_guardians` → 3 permission denials (student grading, parent submitting, teacher writing to a class they don't teach) plus a draft-after-unpublish bonus assertion. All assertions pass; demo state restored at end of run.**

ActivityService hoists Step 4's private `recordActivity()` into a shared writer; CommentService implements visibility filter (admin/assignee see all, requester sees public-only, non-participant 404) with first-staff-comment SLA-stop bump on `first_response_at` and `tkt.ticket.commented` Kafka emit; ProblemService ships 6 admin-only endpoints including the batch-resolve keystone that locks problem + linked active tickets `FOR UPDATE OF t` in one tx, flips problem to RESOLVED with root_cause/resolution/workaround populated, batch-flips matching tickets to RESOLVED + activity rows + per-ticket `tkt.ticket.resolved` emits with `resolvedViaProblemId`. Step 5 live smoke (12 scenarios on tenant_demo) all pass: activity reads cross-persona, comment visibility model + first_response_at bump + Kafka envelope, problem batch-resolve flips T1+T2 leaving already-RESOLVED T3 untouched, 4 permission denials. One iteration issue caught: array DTO fields (`LinkTicketsDto.ticketIds`, `CreateProblemDto.ticketIds`) need `@IsArray()` + `@IsUUID('all', { each: true })` decorators or the global `forbidNonWhitelisted` ValidationPipe silently drops them. Build clean, all 27 ticket routes mapped on boot. Step 6 wires 2 new Kafka consumers — `TicketNotificationConsumer` (notifications module, all 4 `tkt.ticket.*` topics, fan-out matrix per topic with internal-comment-stays-staff-side rule) and `TicketTaskCompletionConsumer` (tasks module, on `tkt.ticket.resolved`, runs UPDATE … RETURNING and emits `task.completed` per flipped auto-task, closing the Step 3 seed → Step 4 emit → DONE-cascade loop). Live verified on `tenant_demo` end-to-end including Redis IN_APP delivery for both requester + assignee. Step 7 ships the helpdesk staff UI — `Helpdesk` launchpad tile gated on `it-001:read` + 3 routes (`/helpdesk`, `/helpdesk/new`, `/helpdesk/[id]`) + 13 React Query hooks + `tickets-format.ts` with `slaUrgency` 4-state helper + LifebuoyIcon + 4 new `ticket.*` notification descriptors in NotificationBell + helpdesk badge counter wired into use-app-badges. Build sizes 7.89/9.96/8.86 kB. Queue with multi-filter + per-row Assign/Vendor modals + SLA-urgency-tinted breached rows; SLA dashboard with stat cards + by-priority histogram + per-category breakdown; tree editor with employee-XOR-role auto-assignment mutex client-side; vendor CRUD with full contact info form. No API changes — sits on the 6 problem endpoints from Step 5.
